name: Combs Intermediate School
historical_names: St. Ferdinand Public School; Florissant School; Combs Elementary School; Combs School
district_operator: Ferguson-Florissant R-II School District (Florissant School District before the 1952 reorganization)
notes: Seed's 1876 opening is plausible: the Missouri Historical Society genealogy index (from Gretchen Crank's 'Reflections of the Florissant Valley', 1990) lists a 'St. Ferdinand Public School' at Washington St. between St. Jacques and St. Jean — the same block as today's Combs at 300 Rue St. Jean — and a district-history summary states the Florissant School District formed in 1871 and built St. Ferdinand Public School in 1876 (repeated on Grokipedia, an AI source, so year kept at 'probable'). The school's own website does not carry a founding year. Combs is 'famous for cherished artifact, the old St. Ferdinand School bell' (nomoz.org school listing), supporting the site lineage. The village public school was staffed by the Sisters of Loretto from the mid-1850s until 1887, when the public school board declined to license them (Florissant Valley Quarterly, July 2024). The origin of the 'Combs' name and when it was adopted were not found. School still operates as Combs Intermediate (grades 3-5).

name: Cross Keys School
historical_names: Cross Keys School; Cross Keys one-room school
district_operator: Florissant-area public school district (predecessor of Ferguson-Florissant R-II, exact district unverified)
notes: Real school, thinly documented online. The Missouri Historical Society genealogy index (from 'Reflections of the Florissant Valley', 1990) places 'Cross Keys School' on New Halls Ferry Road just north of Parker Road — in the old Cross Keys hamlet (which also had a general store and a post office per TownTapestry's Florissant history). The Florissant Valley Quarterly (Oct. 2022) prints a photo captioned 'Don Zykan Sr. in the 8th Grade class at Cross Keys School, Ferguson, 1942', confirming operation at least into 1942. Seed's 'Before 1951' opening and '1950s?' closing could not be verified; the 1950s hint is consistent with the 1952 Ferguson-Florissant R-II consolidation, but no source was found saying when the school closed or what absorbed it. A modern 'Cross Keys Middle School' (14205 Cougar Dr, Florissant 63033, still open) carries the community name but is a different institution — successor left 'unknown' rather than asserting continuity. Recommended human follow-up: Florissant Valley Historical Society files or FFSD records could pin down dates.

name: DeSmet School
historical_names: DeSmet Elementary; De Smet Elementary
notes: PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED: seed says 'Known Ferguson-Florissant school built in 1953' and an aggregated district history (Grokipedia, an AI-generated source that cites a district history) states 'DeSmet Elementary School opened in 1953 as the first new facility post-merger.' However, no independent confirmation was found: no 'DeSmet' school appears on current or recent FFSD rosters (2023-24 and 2026-27 district directories), on Wikipedia's list of former FFSD schools, or in the Missouri Historical Society's index of historic Florissant-area schools ('Reflections of the Florissant Valley'). Searches surface only De Smet Jesuit High School in Creve Coeur (unrelated, est. 1967) and DeSmet Public School in Missoula, MT. The school presumably existed (name honors Fr. Pierre DeSmet, ordained at St. Ferdinand in 1827) but has likely been renamed or closed — candidate renames could not be established. Recommend human follow-up: FFSD records center or Florissant Valley Historical Society should confirm the school, its address, and its fate before Track B spends effort on it.

name: Sacred Heart Catholic School
historical_names: Sacred Heart Parish School; Sacred Heart School (Florissant)
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: the parish's own history page states the first building constructed was the school — a two-story brick building at the corner of Jefferson and St. Louis Streets, opened September 1866; the upper floor served as the convent. Corroborated by the State Historical Society of Missouri finding aid for the Sacred Heart Church of Florissant records (S0052): 'Jesuits established Sacred Heart in 1866... that year, the first combination school and convent opened.' Sisters of St. Joseph taught first, joined/replaced by Sisters of the Most Precious Blood in 1877, who served until 1994. A second two-story classroom/teacherage was added in 1872 (not a separate seed row). The parish school remains open as Sacred Heart Catholic School at 501 St. Louis St (school site live, PK-8), independent of the 2018 All Saints Academy partnership. Building-level lineage is split across ALL-006/007/008. NOTE: the school website (shcs-flo.org/history) prints 'September 15, 1886' for the first day of school — internally inconsistent with its own 'twenty years later in 1866' framing and with the parish history and SHSMO; treated as a typo for 1866.

name: Sacred Heart School - 1866 Building
historical_names: Original Sacred Heart School; Sacred Heart combination school and convent
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: First school building of the Sacred Heart parish school lineage (see ALL-005): two-story brick at Jefferson & St. Louis Sts, opened September 1866 with classrooms below and convent above. When the new school at St. Denis & Jefferson was dedicated November 28, 1889, this building 'remained as a convent for the Sisters' — it ceased school use in 1889 and the convent portion burned in 1903 (replaced 1904 by the convent building still standing at St. Louis & Jefferson). Successor recorded as the 1889 building (ALL-007), which took over classes.

name: Sacred Heart School - 1889 Building
historical_names: Sacred Heart Parish School (1889 building)
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: replacement school at the corner of St. Denis and Jefferson Streets, plans drawn fall 1888, 'solemnly dedicated by the Very Rev. Henry Muehlsiepen, Vicar General of St. Louis, on Thanksgiving Day, November 28, 1889' (parish and school history pages). Upper-grade classes moved to the new St. Louis Street building in 1952 — the basis for 'closed 1952' — but the building did not stop being used for education: the school's own history says it is 'today home for Preschool and Kindergarten students' and 'was also used by the Archdiocesan Special Education Learning Center for over 30 years.' Closed_year kept at 1952 (probable) meaning 'ceased to be the main school,' with the continued PreK/K use noted here.

name: Sacred Heart School - 1952 Building
historical_names: Sacred Heart Catholic School (current building)
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: 'In 1952 it became necessary to build a new school. The corner stone was laid on March 23, 1952. It faced St. Louis Street' (parish history); the school opened for the 1952-53 year per the seed and remains the operating Sacred Heart Catholic School at 501 St. Louis St. Still open (school website active; independent of All Saints Academy).

name: St. Ferdinand School
historical_names: St. Ferdinand Catholic School; St. Ferdinand Parish School; St. Ferdinand Elementary
district_operator: St. Ferdinand Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Resolved seed's 'Unknown' opening: the parish school of St. Ferdinand's dates from 1887 — Gilbert Garraghan's 1923 history (Jesuit Archives, chap. 42) states the parish school 'dates from 1887' and opened September 1887 in temporary quarters in the Sisters' house, and the Florissant Valley Quarterly (July 2024) gives the exact opening as September 5, 1887 after the public school board declined to license the Sisters of Loretto. A permanent parochial schoolhouse at Old St. Ferdinand was built in 1888 (May 1888 bid letter). Older school tradition on the site: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne's girls' school (1819) and the Loretto-staffed village public school (from the 1840s/mid-1850s until 1887) — related institutions, not the parochial school itself. The school moved to the current Charbonier Road campus in 1955 (parish history: first Mass 1955 in the 'combination church and school building'; additions through the 1960s). In 2018 the school merged into the All Saints Academy partnership and its campus became All Saints Academy - St. Ferdinand Campus (ALL-014); recorded closed 2018 as an independent school. St. Sabina and St. Martin de Porres parishes were merged into St. Ferdinand Parish in 2023 (post-dates the school merger).

name: St. Sabina School
historical_names: St. Sabina Parish School; St. Sabina Catholic School
district_operator: St. Sabina Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed verbatim by the (now-merged) parish's surviving history page: 'St. Sabina Parish was founded in 1960... St. Sabina School opened in 1961 and closed in 2010. The parish was merged into St. Ferdinand Parish in 2023.' The church at 1625 Swallow Lane was built as 'a gymnasium attached to a school' and dedicated in 1963 (April 2026 canonical closure decree, St. Louis Review). NUANCE: after the parish school closed, the site hosted 'The Academy at St. Sabina' — an Archdiocese of St. Louis Department of Special Education school for students with special needs (~29-30 students, NCES PSS 2015-16 and 2017-18; still open as of January 2019 per flovalleynews.com). It closed within 2016-2021 per the Feb. 2021 St. Louis Review article on Trinity Catholic. The Academy was a different institution (special-education program), so no successor school_id is recorded; the site detail is noted for whoever surveys yearbooks there.

name: St. Norbert School
historical_names: St. Norbert Catholic School; St. Norbert Parish School
district_operator: St. Norbert Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed by the parish's own history pages: St. Norbert School opened September 1988 with grades K-3 (first principal Sr. Rosalie Wisneski, OSF), added a grade each year, and graduated its first class in 1995. In August 2018 it became part of the All Saints Academy partnership school — its campus is now All Saints Academy - St. Norbert Campus (ALL-013). Parish itself was founded May 18, 1965 (Cardinal Ritter); church first Mass Sept. 3, 1967. MINOR FLAG: seed and the parish use 16455 New Halls Ferry Road; the academy's admissions page prints '16475 New Halls Ferry Rd' — likely a typo on the academy site.

name: All Saints Academy - St. Norbert Campus
historical_names: St. Norbert School (continues as campus)
district_operator: All Saints Academy (partnership of St. Norbert, St. Ferdinand and formerly St. Rose Philippine Duchesne parishes) / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: All Saints Academy was announced January 25, 2018 and opened for the 2018-19 school year as a partnership-model school uniting St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert and St. Rose Philippine Duchesne schools (St. Louis Review, Feb. 2018 and Aug. 2018). The St. Norbert campus continues at the former St. Norbert School site on New Halls Ferry Rd. Still operating — the academy's admissions site lists St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert campuses; the third campus (St. Rose Philippine Duchesne) closed after the 2022-23 year amid enrollment decline (St. Louis Review, June 2023).

name: All Saints Academy - St. Ferdinand Campus
historical_names: St. Ferdinand School (continues as campus)
district_operator: All Saints Academy (partnership of St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert and formerly St. Rose Philippine Duchesne parishes) / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: this is the St. Ferdinand School campus operating under the All Saints Academy partnership since the 2018-19 school year (successor entity to ALL-009). Still operating at 1735 Charbonier Rd (~180 students per the St. Ferdinand parish history page). The third ASA campus, St. Rose Philippine Duchesne, closed in 2023, leaving St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert as the two remaining campuses.

name: North County Christian School
historical_names: North County Day School; North County Christian Academy
district_operator: Private (founded by Ferguson Church of the Nazarene)
notes: SEED ERROR: seed lists opened 1994; the school was actually founded in 1962 as 'North County Day School' by Rev. Udell G. Moss, starting as a kindergarten in the Ferguson Church of the Nazarene basement (one teacher, twelve students). Confirmed by the school's history as republished by the Greater North County Chamber and by a 2012 Florissant Patch article marking its 50th anniversary. It moved to 1309 N. Elizabeth in Ferguson in 1966, then purchased the current 14-acre campus at 845 Dunn Road, Florissant on July 8, 2004 — grades 1-12 moved in within 50 days, preschool/kindergarten followed August 2005, remaining fields acquired 2007. privateschoolreview lists 'Year Founded 1962'. Still operating (PK-12). The seed's 1994 is unexplained — possibly a conflation with a re-incorporation or expansion year.

name: Atonement Lutheran School
historical_names: Atonement Lutheran Church School
notes: Seed's 'Unknown' opening resolved to 1956 (probable): privateschoolreview states 'Established in 1956, Atonement Lutheran School is a non-profit parochial school in Florissant, MO operated by the Lutheran Church of the Atonement.' The congregation itself was founded in 1951 per St. Louis Patina's profile of the church building — consistent with a 1956 school start. Still operating (PK-8, ~220 students per elementaryschools.org; school site alcs-web.com active). SEED ERROR: district/operator listed as 'LCMS' — the school is ELCA (the comparison profile explicitly says 'E.L.C.A.', and the congregation's materials use ELCA branding). One source (MoHistory index, 'Reflections of the Florissant Valley') maps a 'Lutheran Church of the Atonement' at St. Francois at St. Ferdinand St. — an earlier church site; the school/church sit on N. New Florissant Rd today.

name: Grace Christian Academy
historical_names: Grace Christian School; Foundation Christian Academy
district_operator: Private Christian (ministry of Dorsett Village Church since 2012)
notes: Seed's 'Unknown' opening resolved: the school's own history page (fcastl.org) says 'On August 31st, 1981, the doors of Grace Christian School were opened for the very first time' with 96 students. Same address and phone as the NCES 'Grace Christian Academy' listing (2890 Patterson Rd, 314-837-8283; PSS 2023-24, K-8, 54 students) — the school now brands itself 'Foundation Christian Academy' and the legal nonprofit is 'Grace Christian Academy St Louis' (EIN 83-4588278, 501(c)(3) ruling March 2023). Itinerary: opened 1981 → purchased Penn Junction Elementary from Pattonville SD in May 1985 (home for 28 years) → became a ministry of Dorsett Village Church January 2012 → ~4 years in the Briarcrest building (Pattonville) → ~1 year in Overland → moved in 2018 into the Christ First Church facility at 2890 Patterson Rd, Florissant. So the school only arrived at the seed's address in 2018; pre-2018 attendance records would live under earlier names/addresses. Still operating.

name: Marygrove School / Marygrove Services
historical_names: Marygrove; House of the Good Shepherd (St. Louis); Convent of the Good Shepherd
district_operator: Catholic Charities of St. Louis (founded by the Sisters of the Good Shepherd)
notes: The Florissant campus at 2705 Mullanphy Lane was established in 1969 when the Sisters of the Good Shepherd relocated from their Gravois Avenue convent (operated there 1895-1969; the order has served St. Louis since 1849 and counts the institution's heritage to that date). Operated by Catholic Charities of St. Louis since ~1983 (GuideStar EIN 43-1024440, 'Child Center - Marygrove'). The on-campus 'Marygrove School' is a private special-education day school for residents; NCES PSS lists 'Marygrove Services, Inc.' (grades 5-11, nonsectarian) through 2021-22. Organization is still operating (active site, 2024-25 reports), though GuideStar notes residential program consolidation after 2021 - whether the on-campus school still operates as a separate school should be confirmed; the residential program has shrunk. Recommended human follow-up: Catholic Charities program office can confirm current on-campus school status. Note the school serves girls/boys in residential treatment - yearbook output likely minimal or nonexistent.

name: Oak Bridge School
historical_names: Oak Bridge
notes: Small private accredited school (MNSAA) at 3465 Shackelford Rd, Florissant, nursery/6 weeks through grade 6, using a Howard Gardner Multiple Intelligences curriculum. Founding date not found online; earliest hard evidence is its first NCES Private School Universe Survey response for 2017-18 (enrollment 40, dropping to 17 by 2021-22) per ProPublica's private-school demographics tool, and the school's own site copyrighted 2018 - so it was operating by ~2017. Currently open and offering tours (oakbridgeschool.org; listed open on third-party directories).

name: Hazelwood High School - Original (Dunn Road)
historical_names: Hazelwood High School; Original Hazelwood High School
notes: The first Hazelwood High School building, completed 1954 at 1865 Dunn Road in the Spanish Lake area of unincorporated north St. Louis County, per Hazelwood Central HS's own About Us history page (ninth grade initiated in the district in 1954-55 per the stipulated history in United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F. Supp. 1276 (E.D. Mo. 1975)). Seed's closed year of 1965 is off by one: the second Hazelwood High School was built in 1965 and opened in 1966, ending this building's tenure as the district high school - 1966 is the correct 'closed as Hazelwood HS' year. The building was never demolished or idled: it remained a district school and today houses the Hazelwood Opportunity Center (alternative HS program) at the same address (cross-reference: ALL-476 in another batch). SEED ZIP FLAG: 1865 Dunn Road is ZIP 63138 (Spanish Lake), not 63031. This school is also duplicated as ALL-063/ALL-084/ALL-125/ALL-259/ALL-458/ALL-459 elsewhere in the seed data.

name: Hazelwood High School - Second Building (New Halls Ferry)
historical_names: Hazelwood High School
notes: The second Hazelwood High School opened in 1966 at 15875 New Halls Ferry Road with 2,515 students in grades 10-12, per the school's own history page (Wikipedia gives 'built 1965, opened 1966'). It never actually closed: 'Hazelwood High School' here is the same institution as today's Hazelwood Central High School (ALL-022) - the 'Central' designator appeared in 1974 to distinguish it from the new East and West schools (opened 1977), so 1974 is recorded as the year this name/identity ended. Row kept separate from ALL-022 per no-silent-merge rule, but this is a rename, not a replacement. The school was so overcrowded it ran split double shifts in 1970-72.

name: Hazelwood Central High School
historical_names: Hazelwood High School (1966-1974)
notes: Continuation of ALL-021 under the 'Central' name adopted ~1974 when Hazelwood East and West opened (they began classes 1977). Some sources, including Wikipedia's infobox, list 'Established 1954' - that counts the whole Hazelwood High School lineage back to the Dunn Road building (ALL-020), not this campus. Still operating at 15875 New Halls Ferry Rd (NCES ID 291383000622, ~1,718 students 2024-25). Yearbook name: 'Torch'. Duplicated in other batches as ALL-062/ALL-086/ALL-124/ALL-258/ALL-531 (and mislabeled ALL-460 'Dunn Road Campus').

name: Brown School
historical_names: James School; Douglas and James School; Brown School
district_operator: Brown rural school district / Hazelwood School District (from 1950)
notes: One-room rural school on the north side of Old Jamestown Road east of Douglas Rd (near Carrico Rd), per Ch. 1 of Franzwa's 1977 'History of the Hazelwood School District' as excerpted by the Old Jamestown Association. Founded when 'Uncle Billy' James deeded 3/4 acre to the school board on December 9, 1859; the brick school was originally called James School, then Douglas and James, finally Brown School (named for the adjoining Brown family - David, Clement, William). Taken over by the new Hazelwood School District in 1950, after which the building became a residence/parsonage for Salem Baptist Church across the street (still standing). Seed's '1950s?' close is consistent. The modern namesake successor serving the area is Brown Elementary (3325 Chickory Creek Lane, brn.hazelwoodschools.org - matches seed 'Current Address'); it appears in other seed batches as ALL-092/ALL-120. Not merged per no-silent-merge rule.

name: Cold Water School
historical_names: Cold Water School; Coldwater School; Old Cold Water School
district_operator: Cold Water rural school district / Hazelwood School District (from 1950)
notes: County District #2. A log Cold Water School near Vaile & Old Halls Ferry Rd existed by the 1840s (the school the Brown School pupils were walking miles to, per Franzwa ch. 1); it burned in 1850 and the surviving one-room brick building was built in 1859 (150th anniversary celebrated 2009, per the Hazelwood district press release carried by flovalleynews.com). Annexed into Hazelwood School District February 18, 1950; closed spring 1954 per the St. Louis County landmarks page. Building survives as a museum on the HSD Learning Center grounds at 15875 New Halls Ferry Rd, in front of Hazelwood Central HS. Namesake modern successor: Cold Water Elementary, 1105 Wiethaupt Rd (cws.hazelwoodschools.org - matches seed 'Current Address'); appears in other batches as ALL-093/ALL-119. Building-dating nuance: opened_year left unknown because the school entity predates 1859 (the 1859 date is the surviving building).

name: Prigge School / Larimore School
historical_names: Prigge School; Larimore School
district_operator: Prigge (Larimore) rural school district / Hazelwood School District (from 1951)
notes: CONFLATED NAME: 'Prigge' and 'Larimore' are not two schools - per Franzwa's 1977 district history (Ch. 6), 'Prigge is the predecessor name for the Larimore district.' The Prigge district elected to join Hazelwood in a special election on July 29, 1951. Franzwa notes at least three 'Prigge'-annotated schoolhouse sites on a 1927 map (named for Charles F. Prigge family), plus a possible 'colored school' on Prigge land whose location is unrecorded. The school line continued as Larimore; the namesake modern successor is Larimore Elementary, 1025 Trampe Lane (63138, lar.hazelwoodschools.org), appearing in other batches as ALL-464/ALL-534. Closed_year 1951 = end of independent-district operation, not necessarily last day classes met in the building.

name: Hyatt School
historical_names: Hyatt School
district_operator: Hyatt rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: County District #10 per a sibling seed row (ALL-254, 'Closed/Converted'). One of the 13 schoolhouses that became the Hazelwood School District (district press release via flovalleynews.com, 2009). Located on/near Shackelford Road; almost certainly named for the Hyatt family whose farms anchored that area - the Joseph Hyatt House (2625 Shackelford Rd, c.1860) is a St. Louis County landmark. Exact annexation/closure year not found; '1951' recorded as probable = end of the district's 1949-1951 annexation window documented in United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F. Supp. 1276 (E.D. Mo. 1975). Building may have continued as a Hazelwood district school afterward. No namesake modern school.

name: Elm Grove School
historical_names: Elm Grove School; Old Elm Grove School; The Little Red Schoolhouse
district_operator: Elm Grove rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: County District #9; established 1852, one of the earliest school buildings in the county. Closed 1952 'following the organization of the Hazelwood School District' per the City of Hazelwood historical marker; building moved to Brookes Park (450 Brookes Dr, Hazelwood 63042) in 1966 (Esley Hamilton's St. Louis County rural-schools survey says rebuilt in the park 1961 - minor discrepancy) and is preserved as 'The Little Red Schoolhouse,' a county landmark. SEED FLAG: address '450 Brookes Lane' is the relocated-museum site at 450 Brookes Dr, Hazelwood (ZIP 63042, not 63031), not the original school location, which I could not pin down online. A sibling seed row 'Old Elm Grove School' (ALL-249, ZIP 63045, 'Closed/Relocated') is the same school/building.

name: Pea Ridge School
historical_names: Pea Ridge School
district_operator: Pea Ridge rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: Verified as a real school: USGS GNIS 'Pea Ridge School' (N38.810882, W90.195388) appears on the Columbia Bottom, MO topo quad in north St. Louis County (topoquest.com listing). One of the 13 schoolhouses consolidated into the Hazelwood School District 1949-1951 (federal court stipulation, 392 F. Supp. 1276; district press release list via flovalleynews.com). 1951 = end of the documented annexation window; exact school-level closure year not found online. Building no longer stands or is a private residence. No successor school identified - students would have fed Hazelwood district elementaries.

name: Columbia Bottom School
historical_names: Columbia Bottom School
district_operator: Columbia Bottom rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: Named in the Hazelwood district's own 2009 list of the 13 schoolhouses consolidated into the district (via flovalleynews.com) and in the 1949-1951 annexation history stipulated in 392 F. Supp. 1276. Presumably in the Columbia Bottoms/Columbia Bottom Road area at the confluence of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers (northeast corner of the county - the 'Columbia Bottom' USGS quad); no building record or dates found online. 1951 = probable end of independent operation. Nothing further found; likely requires Franzwa's 1977 'History of the Hazelwood School District' (print) or county deed records - recommended human follow-up.

name: Vossenkemper School
historical_names: Vossenkemper School
district_operator: Vossenkemper rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: Verified real: one of the 13 Hazelwood-consolidation schoolhouses (district press release list, flovalleynews.com 2009). Located at Robbins Mill (later Highway 67) near Jamestown per the 1989 St. Louis County North historic buildings inventory (Esley Hamilton, Phase II: Black Jack); also annotated as a family-named school on the 1935 USGS Columbia Bottom topo sheet (pastmaps.com). No operating dates found; '1951' = probable end of independent operation in the 1949-1951 annexation window. Likely named for the Vossenkemper family of the New Bielefeld/Black Jack area.

name: Black Jack School
historical_names: Black Jack School
district_operator: Black Jack rural school district / Hazelwood School District
notes: One of the 13 schoolhouses consolidated into Hazelwood School District (1949-1951 window; court stipulation + district press release list). The community's school lot at what is now Black Jack City Hall (4655 Parker Road) was purchased by the local school board in the 1850s; the surviving 1928 school building at that address is now Black Jack City Hall per the St. Louis County historic buildings inventory. Not to be confused with the Salem Lutheran/Parker Road School (1895, private Lutheran school, county landmark) on the same road. ZIP: Black Jack addresses are 63033, not seed's 63031. No post-consolidation dates found; whether the 1928 building operated as a Hazelwood district school past 1951 is unresolved.

name: McCluer North High School
historical_names: McCluer North
notes: Seed's 1971 opening confirmed: founded 1971 at 705 Waterford Drive (bounded by St. Catherine and Parker Rd, facing the Florissant Civic Center) to relieve the original McCluer High School (built for 3,300, enrollment 4,500+ by 1971 with split sessions); students split into McCluer North and McCluer High Schools beginning with the 1972-73 year per the McCluer HS history. Still operating (mnhs.fergflor.org; 'Stars'). Sister schools elsewhere in the seed: McCluer HS (ALL-111 etc.) and McCluer South-Berkeley HS (ALL-113 etc.).

name: Cross Keys Middle School
historical_names: Cross Keys Junior High School; Cross Keys Jr. High; Cross Keys School
notes: Refined seed's '1960s?' to probable 1960s: the Wedgwood subdivision HOA history states FFSD acquired the land on which the Wedgwood and Cross Keys schools were later built during the subdivision's construction (fall 1963 - May 1967); a classmates.com listing shows a Cross Keys alumnus from 1968-69 and a 1971 'The Padlock' yearbook for 'Cross Keys Jr. High' (grades 6-9) exists. Exact opening year not found online. Operated as Cross Keys Junior High (grades 6-9) before becoming a middle school. The Missouri Historical Society genealogy index lists an earlier 'Cross Keys School' at New Halls Ferry Road just north of Parker Road - a different site ~1 mi south, likely the rural predecessor school the current campus replaced; that lineage is unverified. FFSD's 2027-28 restructuring plan will convert Cross Keys to a 6-8 middle school (fergflor.org board post). Currently operating at 14205 Cougar Drive.

name: Wedgwood 6th Grade Center
historical_names: Wedgwood Elementary School; Wedgewood Elementary School; Wedgwood School
notes: Same land-acquisition evidence as ALL-033: FFSD acquired the Wedgwood school site while the surrounding Wedgwood subdivision was being built (fall 1963 - May 1967), so the school opened in the mid-to-late 1960s; exact year not found. Originally Wedgwood Elementary (K-6); converted to a 6th Grade Center when FFSD reconfigured grades to primary (PreK-2) / intermediate (3-5) / 6th-grade-center / middle (7-8) around 2019-2021 (Wikipedia district article lists it as 'Wedgewood Sixth Grade Center, formerly Wedgwood Elementary School'). Spelling varies: NCES uses 'Wedgwood', Wikipedia and some FFSD materials use 'Wedgewood'. Still operating at 14275 New Halls Ferry Road per NCES (2024-25) and the FFSD 2023-24 directory.

name: Commons Lane Elementary School
historical_names: Commons Lane Primary School; Commons Lane Elementary
school_type: Public Primary School (PreK-2; formerly K-6 elementary)
notes: Currently operating at 2700 Derhake Road - listed in the official FFSD 2023-24 building directory and has its own site (clps.fergflor.org, 'Commons Lane Primary School'). Reconfigured from K-6 elementary to a PreK-2 primary school in FFSD's grade-level restructuring; feeding into an intermediate partner (likely Robinwood). Opening year not found in web sources; the surrounding Derhake subdivisions were built in the early-mid 1960s, suggesting a mid-1960s construction, but no citation found - left unknown.

name: Halls Ferry Elementary School
historical_names: Halls Ferry Intermediate School; Halls Ferry School
school_type: Public Intermediate School (grades 3-5; formerly K-6 elementary)
notes: Currently operating at 13585 New Halls Ferry Road (FFSD 2023-24 directory; 2018-19 parent handbook at resources.finalsite.net). Now serves grades 3-5 as 'Halls Ferry Intermediate School' after FFSD's grade reconfiguration (Wikipedia district article). Opening year not found online. Note: the Halls Ferry name traces to the 19th-century Hall's Ferry route; a different rural 'Halls Ferry'-area school lineage may exist in the historical record but was not verified.

name: Jury Elementary School
historical_names: Jury School
notes: Operating at 11950 Old Halls Ferry Road - listed as school #26 on the official Hazelwood School District map/directory (City of Hazelwood document center) and reported in flovalleynews as an active school in 2009+. Jury is NOT one of the 13 rural schoolhouses that formed Hazelwood SD in 1949-51 (per the district's 150th-anniversary Coldwater School article listing them: Brown, Coldwater, Vossenkemper, Pea Ridge, Columbia Bottom, Prigge, Twillman, Black Jack, Elm Grove, Hyatt, Rosary, Garrett, Bonfils), so it is a post-consolidation building; the 'Jury School' former name suggests it may continue an older rural Jury district/school name, but no founding date found - left unknown.

name: Jamestown Elementary School

name: Our Lady of Fatima School
historical_names: Our Lady of Fatima Catholic School
district_operator: Our Lady of Fatima Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis

The property sold for $1.6M in 2005: Johnny Londoff Chevrolet bought the site; Lindenwood University bought the church/school building for its North County campus (archbalt.org, Jan. 2012; flovalleynews, Mar. 2008 - the reuse is the separate seed row ALL-076). name: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School
historical_names: St. Thomas the Apostle School; St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Catholic School
district_operator: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis

notes: LINEAGE: the school at 3500 St. Catherine Street was originally St. Thomas the Apostle School (St. Thomas the Apostle Parish, founded 1960 - stlgs.org / closedparishes.com). In 2005 the parish merged with St. Dismas and Our Lady of Fatima (north of I-270) to form St. Rose Philippine Duchesne Parish; Archbishop Burke's announcement specified 'the school for the new parish will be at the current St. Thomas the Apostle School' (STLPR, May 2005), so the school was renamed St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School at that site (confirmed at 3500 St. Catherine in the 2017-18 MNSAA accredited-schools list). In 2018 the school joined St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert schools under the new All Saints Academy governance partnership (St. Louis Review) - recorded here as closed 2018 with successor ALL-048 (All Saints Academy - St. Rose campus, a separate seed row in batch04). That campus itself closed after the 2022-23 school year due to enrollment decline (St. Louis Review, June 2023); the parish was subsumed into Sacred Heart Parish, Florissant, on Aug. 1, 2023 under the 'All Things New' plan. NOTE: ALL-108 (batch05) is a cross-batch duplicate of successor ALL-048.

name: All Saints Academy - St. Rose Philippine Duchesne

Predecessor parish school on this site: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne School (ALL-047 in batch03), formed 2005 from the merger of the St. Thomas the Apostle and St. Dismas elementary schools (flovalleynews.com/?p=13919). DATA-QUALITY FLAG: seed row ALL-108 'All Saints Academy - St. Rose Campus' in batch05 is the same entity under a duplicate row - coordinator should reconcile. The parish itself (St. Rose Philippine Duchesne, formed 2005) was merged into Sacred Heart Parish in August 2023 under All Things New.

name: St. Thomas the Apostle School
historical_names: St. Thomas the Apostle Catholic School; St. Thomas School
district_operator: St. Thomas the Apostle Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: SEED ADDRESS ERROR: seed lists '5300 Derby Lane' - no Derby Lane exists in Florissant; the parish and school were at 3500 St. Catherine St (Archdiocese closed-parishes list, St. Louis Genealogical Society, NCES-derived Education Bug listing all agree). Parish founded 1960 (formed from Our Lady of Fatima and St. Dismas territory); K-8 school documented at that address in NCES-derived records (~277 students). Opening year not found online; school likely dates to the early-mid 1960s alongside the parish (founded 1960, church built 1966). Per St. Louis Review (Jan 2023), the current St. Rose school building previously housed Prep Seminary North, and 'the old St. Thomas School next door is now St. Catherine Retirement Community.'

name: St. Christopher School

In the 2005 consolidation the parish was suppressed: territory north of I-270 joined St. Angela Merici Parish in Florissant (school = ALL-080, batch05; St. Angela Merici's own parish history confirms it 'welcomed its newest members from Transfiguration and St. Christopher' in July 2005), while territory south of I-270 merged with four other parishes into Holy Name of Jesus Parish, whose students attended the new Christ, Light of the Nations School at the former St. John Neumann site in Spanish Lake (itself closed 2020). So the school closed with its parish in 2005 (probable - closure documented at parish level, school disposition inferred) and students split between ALL-080 and Christ, Light of the Nations (not in dataset). The school's own opening year not found; likely mid-1960s-1970s alongside the parish (founded 1967). The site later housed a 'St. Christopher Learning Center' (Archdiocese special-education site; see ALL-056 notes).

name: Salem Lutheran School
historical_names: Salem Lutheran School; Salem Evangelical Lutheran School
notes: Corrected seed's 1895 (that is the one-room schoolhouse building date - see ALL-052). Per the congregation's own history: Salem Lutheran Church was organized November 1849 in New Bielefeld (now Black Jack), 'a school was organized soon after the church was established' with the pastor as teacher, and the first regular teacher (G. A. Just) was called in 1868 - 'school has been conducted without interruption to this day.' The founding year could be as early as ~1850; 1868 is the first firmly dated operation. Currently operating: re-enrollment open for 2026-27, PK-8, ~43 students (peak ~200 in the 2010s). Campus at 5180-5195 Parker Rd, Black Jack (mailing address Florissant 63033). Seed note about a 2026 all-school reunion is consistent with an active alumni association.

name: Salem Lutheran School - Original Building

Per the church's own history it was built in 1895 across the street from the church and 'used as a classroom until 1950,' after which instruction continued in the school's newer facilities - so 'opened/closed' here are building-use dates for the same continuous school as ALL-051, which the seed deliberately split as an archival target. The 'Old School House' still stands, was designated a Historic Building of St. Louis County in 1970, and is used for youth group/Bible classes/applebutter canning. Note the county survey once incorrectly identified it as a public school. Kept as separate row per no-silent-merge rule; recommend coordinator treat as a campus of ALL-051.

Opened_year 1966 = conversion of the old high school to Kirby JH (probable - exact conversion year inferred from Central HS's 1966 opening; schooldesigns.com describes the building's high-school-to-junior-high-to-middle-school history). name: Prigge/Larimore School
historical_names: Prigge School; Larimore School; Prigge School District (Larimore district)
district_operator: Prigge/Larimore rural school district (St. Ferdinand Township) / Hazelwood School District (after 1951)
notes: Rural one-school district of St. Ferdinand Township named for Charles F. Prigge; at least three schoolhouses carried the Prigge name on a 1927 district map, so a single founding date is not meaningful. Per Gregory Franzwa's History of the Hazelwood School District (1977), quoted at pipes.family: 'Prigge is the predecessor name for the Larimore district, which elected to join the growing Hazelwood School District in a special election on July 29, 1951.' That merger is corroborated by the pretrial stipulation in United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F.Supp. 1276 (E.D. Mo. 1975) — the district formed from thirteen rural districts between 1949 and 1951. The seed's 'Closed 1950s?' reflects the district merger, not a school closure: the school continued under Hazelwood and the lineage persists as Larimore Elementary (1025 Trampe Lane, 63138), which is the separate current-school row ALL-464 — recorded here as successor in the modern-entity sense. The exact date the school/district name changed from Prigge to Larimore was not found (Franzwa's book, not digitized, is the likely source). FLAG: duplicate coverage — same entity also appears as ALL-025 and ALL-096 ('Prigge/Larimore School', 63031/63034) and ALL-251 ('Prigge/Larimore School #6', the 1910 county district number).

name: Twillman School
historical_names: Twillman School; Twillman School District

notes: Rural school of the Twillman district in St. Ferdinand Township, named for the Twillman(n) family — the John Henry Twillman House (built 1870, St. Louis County landmark) stands across the street at 11840 Bellefontaine Rd and spanishlakemo.org confirms 'the school across the street is named for the family.' The district was one of the thirteen rural districts merged into Hazelwood 1949-1951 (United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F.Supp. 1276). Twillman Elementary's own website brands the school 'Roaring To Excellence Since 1927' — used as probable opened_year; seed row ALL-467 ('Twillman School - 1928 Building', in another batch) corroborates a ~1927-28 building on the Bellefontaine Rd site, and ALL-466 'Twillman Schoolhouse' suggests an earlier schoolhouse. The school never closed: it continues as Twillman Elementary (11831 Bellefontaine Rd, 63138), which is the separate current-school row ALL-465 — recorded as successor in the modern-entity sense. The seed's 'Closed 1950s?' reflects the district merger, not a school closure.

name: Jana Elementary School

Students went virtual, then were redistricted to other Hazelwood elementaries starting Nov 28, 2022 (AP); the district confirmed in March 2023 there is 'no expectation that Jana Elementary will reopen' (FOX2). In 2024 the board renamed the building the 'Hazelwood School District Logistics Center' (Wikipedia). No single successor school — students dispersed across district elementaries; receiving-school assignments not published. Physical address 405 Jana Drive is in 63031, not 63034 (borderline-ZIP row, retained per instructions).

notes: All Saints Academy opened in 2018 under a multi-campus model jointly operated by its sponsoring parishes and the Archdiocese (St. Louis Review). It operated on three Florissant campuses: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne (3500 St. Catherine St, 63033 — the former parish school site), St. Norbert, and St. Ferdinand. Citing enrollment decline (238 K-8 students in 2018 falling to 131 registered for fall 2023) and staffing vacancies, the St. Rose campus closed for the 2023-24 school year; the archdiocese's Find-a-School page now lists it as 'CLOSED.' Students were offered transfer to the continuing St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert campuses — the institutional successor is All Saints Academy itself, which persists on its two remaining campuses (seed rows ALL-013 'St. Norbert Campus' and ALL-014 'St. Ferdinand Campus' cover those sites). FLAG: this row is the same entity as ALL-048 ('All Saints Academy - St. Rose Philippine Duchesne', 63033) and ALL-135 (63042) — same school at different seed ZIPs; kept separate per no-silent-merge rule.

name: McCluer High School

Wikipedia's infobox gives 'Established 1957' while the article text says it 'opened in 1958' as a junior high — hence probable rather than confirmed; the school converted to a senior high in 1962 when Ferguson High School closed (yearbook lineage likely continuous). The campus also holds the historic Taille de Noyer house, relocated there in 1960. Related rows in other batches: ALL-116 'McCluer High School - Original' and ALL-438 'McCluer Junior High School' (the same early McCluer), and ALL-032/ALL-112 'McCluer North High School' — a different school, fuzzy-name match only.

name: McCluer South-Berkeley High School
historical_names: McCluer South-Berkeley High School; MSB; STEAM Academy at McCluer South-Berkeley (2019-)

SURPRISE: seed's 'Opened: 1976' is wrong — that date approximates the 1975-76 court-ordered Berkeley/Kinloch merger into FFSD, not this school's founding. Seed's 'Status: Closed/Reorganized' refers to the October 2018 board redistricting that transformed MSB into the 'STEAM Academy at McCluer South-Berkeley' magnet school (still operating; Wikipedia lists 2022-23 enrollment of 437). name: Berkeley High School
historical_names: Kinloch High School (1937, briefly); Berkeley Senior High School; Berkeley High School
district_operator: Berkeley School District (1937-1975) / Ferguson-Florissant School District (1975-2003)
notes: Per the Wikipedia Berkeley, Missouri article (sourcing city history): the Berkeley School District formed in 1937 after a dispute over the location of a school for Black students; the new district took over Kinloch High School, which had opened that year, and renamed it Berkeley High School (whites only). A newer campus later opened elsewhere and the original building became Berkeley Middle School. On June 7, 1975 a U.S. district court ordered Ferguson-Florissant to annex the Berkeley and Kinloch districts (effective 1975-76; corroborated by the St. Louis American and the St. Louis County historic-schools survey by Esley Hamilton, stlouisarchitecture.org). The former Berkeley High closed December 2003 due to Lambert-St. Louis International Airport expansion and was replaced by McCluer South-Berkeley High School (ALL-113), which opened January 2004 — direct successor, confirmed. Several campus-variant rows exist in other batches: ALL-378, ALL-379 (Hancock Campus), ALL-380 (Caroline Avenue Campus), ALL-381 (Walter Avenue Campus), plus related ALL-383 Berkeley Middle School and ALL-400 Berkeley School District — all kept separate.

name: Central High School
historical_names: Central School (high school department); Ferguson School
notes: SEED CORRECTION: seed says closed '1950s' and places it in the 'Florissant area' (ZIP 63042) — the documented school is at 201 Wesley Ave, Ferguson 63135. 'Central High School' is best read as the high school program of Central School: the St. Louis County Landmarks page records that Ferguson School (built 1877-80) created a two-year high school program in 1896 and expanded it to one of the first accredited four-year public high schools in St. Louis County in 1903 (when the school was renamed Central School). High school students transferred to the new John M. Vogt High School when it opened in 1930; the Landmarks page dates Central School's reversion to elementary status to the new high school's construction in 1931 — the two sources differ by a year, so 1930-31 is the real window. Successor recorded as Vogt High School (seed row ALL-420); the lineage then ran Vogt HS (1930) -> Ferguson High School (1939, ALL-416/417). Row kept separate per no-silent-merge rule, but overlaps ALL-423 'Central School' and ALL-424 'Central School - Early Ferguson School' in the wider dataset — the building lineage is the same school.

name: Central Primary School

Old Halls Ferry addresses are Hazelwood/Florissant territory, not this school. Continuous operation since 1880 in the 1877-80 building (original Ferguson School, renamed Central School 1903; National Register-listed 1984, nomination NPS 84002706). STLPR (2017) documented that FFSD floated closing it. IMPORTANT FUTURE FLAG: FFSD's 2027-28 restructuring announcement states 'Central Primary will close' (fergflor.org board post) — planned closure, not yet in effect as of research date. Currently grades PK-2 paired with an intermediate school.

name: Pattonville High School
historical_names: Pattonville High School
notes: Seed data confirmed by the district's own history page: bond issue April 1934, construction began spring 1935, ~76 students moved into the new building at 11055 St. Charles Rock Road (Banks Rd & St. Charles Rock Rd) on March 17, 1936; first commencement June 18, 1937 (2 graduates). Fully NCA-accredited 1946. Relocated to the current campus at 2497 Creve Coeur Mill Road, Maryland Heights, in 1971 (formally dedicated Jan. 7, 1973); incorporated into Maryland Heights in Dec. 1994 after a boundary exchange with Champ. Yearbook name: Echo (per Wikipedia). Still operating. This row is the continuing school institution; ALL-149 is its original building and ALL-198 (another batch) is the current campus.

name: Pattonville High School - Original Campus
historical_names: Pattonville High School (11055 St. Charles Rock Road building)
notes: Building/campus row for the original PHS at 11055 St. Charles Rock Road, St. Ann (actual ZIP 63074, not 63043). Occupied March 17, 1936; ceased operating as the high school when the school relocated to Creve Coeur Mill Road in 1971. Yearbooks 1936-1970 should be searched under Pattonville High School — this is the same institution, not a successor school (successor_school_id points at the institution row ALL-148 for that reason). The site is now the Holman Middle School campus: Holman Junior High School opened at this address in 1956 while PHS still occupied it, and the Pattonville Learning Center (11097 St. Charles Rock Rd) was built in 1995 on the former football field (Chedester Field). The exact disposition of the 1936 building (demolished vs. incorporated) is not stated in district sources — possible human follow-up with district facilities records.

name: Pattonville Heights Middle School

Name combines 'Pattonville' and 'Maryland Heights'. In January 1967 it became the first school or college in Missouri with a planetarium/observatory in its building. Became a junior high when the new high school opened in 1971; became Pattonville Heights Middle School in 1982. Still operating.

name: Academy of Innovation at Remington

district_operator: Maryland Heights School District (1955-1962) / Pattonville R-III School District (1962- )
notes: Seed confirmed by district history: opened 1955 at 102 Fee Fee Road as Remington Elementary, built by the Maryland Heights School District (first principal Carroll E. Naves; named for teacher Mabel Brewster Remington, d. 1952). Continued as a Pattonville elementary after the Maryland Heights district merged into Pattonville in 1962. Became Remington Traditional School (K-8 school of choice) in 1982; renamed Academy of Innovation at Remington beginning 2024-25 to reflect a learner-centered model. Still operating — same school lineage throughout, name changes only.

name: Parkwood Elementary School
historical_names: Parkwood School

historical_names: Rose Acres School
notes: Seed confirmed by district history: opened 1967 at 2905 Rose Acres Lane, Maryland Heights — a 28-room school built on 11 acres to serve new home construction and relieve crowding at Penn-Junction, Parkwood and Bridgeway elementaries; dedicated Jan. 15, 1968; first principal Wayne Cashion. Still operating.

name: Holy Spirit Catholic School
historical_names: Holy Spirit School; St. Blaise School (probable predecessor name)
district_operator: Holy Spirit Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis (site was St. Blaise Parish until 2004)

In May 2004 St. Blaise merged with St. Lawrence the Martyr (Bridgeton) and St. Mary's (Bridgeton) to form Holy Spirit Parish, which occupies the former St. Blaise site at 3130 Parkwood Lane — the school then took the Holy Spirit name. St. Jude (Overland) parishioners were absorbed later under 'All Things New'. Still operating, ~219 students PK-8 per NCES PSS. Recommended human follow-up: Archdiocese of St. Louis archives could confirm whether the school building dates to St. Blaise's 1961-62 founding or later.

name: McKelvey Elementary School
historical_names: McKelvey Elementary School
notes: Resolved seed's 'Unknown': GBIG building record lists year constructed 1966 for 1751 McKelvey Road, and the school hosted a 'McKelvey's 50th Anniversary' booklet (mckelveyprimary.parkwayschools.net) consistent with a 1966 founding — probable pending a district dedication record. Closure is a renaming/restructuring rather than a true closure: per West Newsmagazine (Dec. 2019), Parkway built a new McKelvey Primary (K-2) at 12657 Fee Fee Rd and converted the existing McKelvey Elementary into a grades 3-5 school; by the 2021-22 year NCES and district directories list 'McKelvey Intermediate' at 1751 McKelvey Rd and 'McKelvey Primary' at the new site — no school named McKelvey Elementary operates there now. Both names appear in Parkway's 2021 salary data, so the split took effect by the 2021-22 school year. Relationship to ALL-158: same building and continuing student body — this is a rename + grade-band reconfiguration, not a new school. Still operating.

name: POSITIVE School
historical_names: Positive School; POS (Pattonville Occupational School Including Technical Individualized Vocational Education)
notes: Seed confirmed by district history: opened in the 1981-82 school year (124 students, 9 staff; first principal George Ruh) as an alternative school to prevent dropouts. POSITIVE = 'Pattonville Occupational School Including Technical Individualized Vocational Education'. Began at the high school, moved in 1982 to the former Penn-Junction Elementary building (closed 1982-83; sold to Grace World Outreach May 1985), and is now housed in a wing of Pattonville High School — the PHS administration page currently lists an assistant principal for Positive School. Not a degree-granting separate campus; likely produces no standalone yearbook — search under Pattonville High School materials.

name: Maryland Heights School
historical_names: Maryland Heights Grade School; Maryland Heights High School
district_operator: Maryland Heights School District (founded as Rural District 24)
notes: Seed confirmed by Pattonville district history: designed by Joseph Senne, built by Daly for $20,000, dedicated September 1924 at 115 Harding, Maryland Heights — six rooms, four teachers, 140 students. The building became Maryland Heights High School. After voters twice rejected it, the Maryland Heights School District merged into Pattonville in 1962; the district at merger consisted of this high school plus Remington Elementary and Carver Elementary (a segregated Negro school, discontinued at merger). Per district history, Maryland Heights high school students 'began attending Pattonville High School' — hence successor ALL-148; elementary continuity runs through Remington (ALL-151). The 115 Harding building became the Pattonville Administration Building until the Learning Center opened in 1995. A March 1939 'Maryland Hi-Lites' school newsletter exists in the Missouri Historical Society Schools Collection (Box 3) — useful human follow-up for yearbook-era documentation.

name: Maryland Heights High School - Gymnasium
historical_names: Pattonville Administration/Printing Facility; Maryland Heights High School gymnasium

notes: FACILITY ROW, NOT A SCHOOL: this is the gymnasium of Maryland Heights High School (seed row ALL-163 in another batch) at 115 Harding Ave; no yearbook research should attach to it. District history confirms the gymnasium was built in 1951 for $40,000 and survived as the Pattonville printing facility after the main 1924 school building was demolished in 1998. Under Proposition S, the printing department moved to the renovated Holman Gym B (new Transportation Building/Print Shop completed ~June 2025), and the district states 'the current printing facility will be demolished and used for additional parking at [Pattonville] Heights' — consistent with the seed's 'demolished July 2025,' hence probable rather than confirmed on the exact date.

name: Carver School for Negroes

notes: Umbrella entity for the segregated Black elementary school operated by the Maryland Heights School District — the same school as campus rows ALL-166 (Adie Road) and ALL-167 (Harding Avenue); kept separate per no-silent-merge rule, but ALL-166+ALL-167 are the two physical sites of this single school. Pattonville's official district history confirms: at the 1962 merger the Maryland Heights district consisted of Maryland Heights High School, Remington Elementary, and 'Carver Elementary for Negroes,' and 'Carver was discontinued.' Opening date not found — the school predates the 1951 Harding Ave building (it replaced an earlier Adie Road building of unknown age). After 1962 the students were presumably absorbed into Pattonville elementaries (most plausibly Remington Elementary, ALL-151, nearby) but no source documents the receiving school. Recommended human follow-up: Missouri History Museum or St. Louis County Library African American schools holdings for the school's founding date; the St. Louis County Library Black Heritage Trail index references 'Carver Elementary School, Maryland Heights, Mo.' (pp. 73-74) in an unnamed source volume.

The school itself continued at ALL-167 — this row tracks the Adie Road building, which ceased use as the school in 1951. When the Adie Road facility itself was built could not be determined online.

Receiving school(s) for Carver students after 1962 are not documented; Remington Elementary (ALL-151) is the geographic candidate. Seed's dates confirmed.

name: Penn School
historical_names: Penn School (Creve Coeur Mill Road)
notes: Seed's unknowns resolved by Pattonville's official history: a white-frame Penn School was erected circa 1850 on modern-day Creve Coeur Mill Road on Fee Fee Creek ('at about the same time the Fee Fee School opened' in 1850 — hence probable, not a documented exact year). A new brick Penn building opened in 1924. In 1936 Penn School and Junction School (ALL-169) merged to form Penn-Junction School (ALL-170); the Penn building was torn down. Mabel Brewster Remington (namesake of Remington Elementary) began teaching at Penn School in 1894.

name: Junction School

Merged with Penn School (ALL-168) in 1936 to form Penn-Junction School (ALL-170). Note the seed's '67' length field is junk (1869-1936 = 67 years is coincidental length arithmetic, not data).

name: Penn-Junction School
historical_names: Penn-Junction Elementary School; POSITIVE School (reuse of building)
notes: Created by the 1936 Penn + Junction merger; located on Branneky Lane at McKelvey Road (later called Penn Junction Road). Seed's 'closed 1950' reflects the district annexation — Penn-Junction School District was annexed into Pattonville in May 1950, but the school itself kept operating as Penn-Junction Elementary under Pattonville (still one of five elementaries in 1956) until the 1982 district reorganization closed it effective the 1982-83 school year. The building reopened as the district's POSITIVE School (dropout-prevention program) and the board approved its sale to Grace World Outreach in May 1985. Students after 1982 were rezoned among remaining Pattonville elementaries; no single successor school.

name: Mount Pleasant School
historical_names: Mount Pleasant Schoolhouse; Mount Pleasant Elementary School
district_operator: Mount Pleasant School District / Pattonville R-III (after 1951)
notes: Seed's 'closed 1951' reflects the district merger, not the school's end. Pattonville's official history: Mount Pleasant Schoolhouse was established in 1836 by Absolom Link east of the Fee Fee community (near modern Midland and Lindbergh); a new brick building went up in 1884 at 11050 N. Warson Road (the district history also says it 'later opened in 1889 as Mount Pleasant Elementary School,' an internal inconsistency — 1836 founding recorded as probable). The Mount Pleasant district merged with Pattonville in 1951, after which the school ran as Mount Pleasant Elementary until it was one of three schools closed in 1978 for declining enrollment. The building was sold to Christian Academy of Greater St. Louis in 1981. In 1965 Mount Pleasant Elementary was the first school west of the Mississippi to use closed-circuit television for instruction.

name: Pattonville Grade School
historical_names: Pattonville Grade School (1907 building); Pattonville Elementary School (possible later name)
district_operator: Fee Fee District No. 16 / School District of Pattonville (after 1930) / Pattonville R-III (after 1951)
notes: IDENTITY AMBIGUITY: the 1907 two-room brick 'Pattonville Grade School' at 4020 Fee Fee Road (south of I-70) replaced the 1850 Fee Fee School and was expanded 1925-27; it served grades 1-8 until Pattonville High School opened in 1936, then K-6, and appears as 'Pattonville Grade School' on the district's 1956 elementary list. The district history separately lists 'Pattonville Elementary School (opened 1954)' as one of three schools closed in 1978 and sold in June 1981 — the grade school building 'later became the Vantage Credit Union.' The most coherent reading is that the grade school was renamed/replaced as Pattonville Elementary in ~1954 (which would explain the seed's 'closed 1950s'), but the district source never says so explicitly, so the 1978 closure is recorded as probable. This row may warrant merging with a future 'Pattonville Elementary School' row if another batch produces one. Students dispersed to remaining Pattonville elementaries after 1978.

name: Bridgeton Elementary School

District history: Bridgeton Elementary opened in 1953 as a two-story eight-classroom building on 3 acres at 11623 Natural Bridge Road in Bridgeton (two rooms, office and storage added 1956); it was one of three schools closed in 1978 for declining enrollment, and the board approved its sale to the First Korean Presbyterian Church of St. Louis in May 1985. Context: the Bridgeton school district was annexed into Pattonville during the 1949-50 school year — so the 1953 building was constructed under Pattonville; whether an older Bridgeton town-school building served in the interim (the Bridgeton Academy/Moravian School lineage reaches back to 1806) is unresolved and is the likely source of the seed's 'Bridgeton School' alias. Successor: none single; students dispersed to remaining Pattonville elementaries.

The board voted to close the school effective the 1982-83 school year under the K-5/middle-school reorganization, and in September 1982 the sole sale bid came from Hope Lutheran Church. Seed's unknown/unknown partially resolved (close year only). Physical ZIP is 63074, not 63043.

name: Bridgeway Elementary School
historical_names: Bridgeway School
notes: Seed's 1963 confirmed: opened fall 1963 at 11635 Oakbury Court, Bridgeton, with Howard Graves as first principal; named for the Bridgeway subdivision. Still operating — listed on the district's current schools page and NCES. Actual ZIP is 63044, not 63043.

name: Briar Crest Elementary School
historical_names: Briar Crest School; Pattonville Early Childhood Center (2018 reuse)
notes: Seed's 'closed 2018' corrected to 2013. District history: built 1964-65 with funds from a Jan. 26, 1965 bond issue; opened fall 1965 and dedicated Dec. 6, 1965, at 2900 Adie Road, St. Ann; first principal Nelson Smith; name from a school-naming contest. The school closed in 2013 due to budget cuts and was leased to a private school and the YWCA, then reopened in August 2018 as the Pattonville Early Childhood Center (Dr. Mary Krekeler, first director of early childhood) — so 2018 is the reuse date, not a closure. The building also housed the first Pattonville school breakfast program (1985). No successor school; the building continues in district use. Actual ZIP is 63074.

name: Carrollton Oaks Elementary School
historical_names: Carrollton Oaks School
notes: Seed's 'closed 2002' corrected to 2001. District history: opened September 1967 with 18 classrooms at 4385 Holmford, Bridgeton (6.5 acres adjacent to the Carrollton Oaks subdivision), built to relieve overcrowding at Carrollton, Bridgeton, Remington, Bridgeway and Pattonville elementaries; dedicated Jan. 8, 1968; first principal James Edwards. One of two Pattonville schools closed in 2001 for the Lambert-St. Louis International Airport expansion (new runway); the building was torn down after closure. Successor confirmed as Drummond Elementary School — built with airport funds as the replacement for both Carrollton and Carrollton Oaks elementaries; closing principal Jim Schwab became Drummond's principal. Drummond Elementary has no row in the seed dataset, so successor_school_id is 'unknown'; it is a current Pattonville elementary in Bridgeton (63044). NOTE: a separate seed row 'Carrollton Elementary School' (ALL-180, different batch) is the *other* school closed by the same 2001 airport expansion — do not conflate the two.

name: Carrollton Elementary School
historical_names: Carrollton School
notes: Pattonville's own history page states Carrollton opened in 1960 at 3936 Celburne in Bridgeton (K-4 in year one, 5th grade added later). It was bought out by St. Louis Lambert International Airport for the west runway expansion and torn down. Closure-year conflict: the district's school-profile list says 'closed in 2001' and Wikipedia says 'shut down in 2002'; the district's by-the-years timeline says the redistricting 'took effect in the 2002-2003 school year when Carrollton and Carrollton Oaks elementary schools closed', so the last operating year was 2001-2002 and 2002 is recorded here. Successor confirmed: former Carrollton students went to Robert Drummond Elementary (ALL-264), opened August 2002 with airport funds as the joint replacement for Carrollton and Carrollton Oaks. DATA-QUALITY FLAG: distinct from ALL-179 'Carrollton Oaks Elementary School' (opened 1967 at 4385 Holmford, Bridgeton) flagged in data/schools_seed_deduped_review_needed.json - same fate but a different building; do not merge.

district_operator: Fee Fee District No. 16 / School District of Pattonville
notes: ENTITY RESOLUTION: the seed's 'Pattonville School District - Original District School' (with note that 'the district consisted of one grade school in the early 1930s') resolves to Pattonville Grade School at 4020 Fee Fee Road, the district's sole grade school. Seed's 'Opened: 1930' is actually the district's reorganization year (April 1930 special election converting Fee Fee District No. 16 into the 'School District of Pattonville, St. Louis County'); the school building itself opened in 1907, a two-room brick school replacing the 1850/1880 Fee Fee School across the road. Still operating under the 'Pattonville Grade School' name in the district's 1956 school list. The district's school list separately records 'Pattonville Elementary School (opened 1954)' on Fee Fee Road near St. Charles Rock Road - most likely the same site/lineage rebuilt or renamed, since the grade school was already listed in 1956 and the addresses are effectively the same; treated here as one continuous school that closed in 1978 (declining enrollment; building sold to Raymond Oetting, June 1981). Wikipedia states Pattonville Elementary 'was replaced by Parkwood Elementary starting in the 1967 school year', so students were progressively redistributed; no single successor school_id is recorded (Parkwood Elementary is outside this batch). The 4020 Fee Fee Rd building later became Vantage Credit Union.

name: Maryland Heights School District (Rural District 24)
historical_names: Maryland Heights School District; Rural District 24; School District No. 24 of St. Louis County
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT ROW - confirmed seed data via Pattonville's own district history: 'The Maryland Heights School District was founded as Rural District 24 in 1924 and was reorganized as a town district.' In 1962, after twice rejecting merger, voters elected to merge with Pattonville R-3. At merger the district comprised: (1) Maryland Heights High School, 115 Harding Ave (building opened Sept 1924 as Maryland Heights School, designed by Joseph Senne, 6 rooms/140 students; later became the Pattonville Administration Building, vacated 1995, demolished 1998) - high school students began attending Pattonville High School; (2) Remington Elementary (opened 1955, remained open); (3) Carver Elementary School for Negroes (discontinued after the merger). The district had no yearbook of its own - search the member schools instead. Corroborating legal record: 'State ex rel. School District No. 24 of St. Louis County v. Neaf', 344 Mo. 905 (Mo. Sup. Ct. 1939) shows District No. 24 operating in the 1930s. Not an individual school for yearbook purposes.
