historical_names: Pattonville Consolidated School District R-3; School District of Pattonville, St. Louis County
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT ROW - a district name era, not a physical school. Pattonville reorganized at a special election on Oct. 27, 1951, when the Junction and Mount Pleasant districts merged in (Penn and Bridgeton districts had already been annexed during the 1949-1950 school year); Pattonville officially became known as the R-3 District and is documented under the name 'Pattonville Consolidated School District R-3' in the 1950s (e.g., a district bus photo caption in the district history). In 1958 the name was changed to 'Pattonville R-3 School District, St. Louis County' - recorded as successor ALL-184. The underlying district organization itself dates to April 1930 (Fee Fee District No. 16 reorganized as the School District of Pattonville). No yearbook search should target this row directly; redirect to member schools.

name: Pattonville R-3 School District
historical_names: Pattonville R-III; Pattonville Consolidated School District R-3 (1951-1958); School District of Pattonville, St. Louis County (1930-1951)
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT ROW - current operating district (umbrella identity, not a school). Name adopted 1958; the continuous district organization itself began April 1930 ('School District of Pattonville, St. Louis County', from Fee Fee District No. 16) and absorbed Penn & Bridgeton (1949-50), Junction & Mount Pleasant (1951 reorganization to R-3), and Maryland Heights School District/Rural District 24 (1962, see ALL-182). Current member schools per psdr3.org: Pattonville High School (ALL-198), Pattonville Heights Middle School, Holman Middle School, Drummond Elementary (ALL-264), Bridgeway Elementary, Parkwood Elementary, Rose Acres Elementary, Willow Brook Elementary, Academy of Innovation at Remington, Pattonville Early Childhood Center (ALL-266), POSITIVE School. Historic member schools no longer operating include Pattonville Grade School/Elementary (ALL-181), Carrollton (ALL-180), Carrollton Oaks, Bridgeton Elementary, St. Ann Elementary, Penn-Junction, Mount Pleasant. Redirect all yearbook-search effort to those member schools; the district publishes no yearbook of its own.

name: Pattonville High School
historical_names: Pattonville High School
notes: This row represents the current campus at 2497 Creve Coeur Mill Road, opened in 1971 (construction completed in phases Sept 1970-Dec 1971; formally dedicated Jan 7, 1973) and still operating (phs.psdr3.org). The school entity itself is older: Pattonville's first high school was established at its original site in 1936 at 11055 St. Charles Rock Road (students moved in March 17, 1936; first commencement June 18, 1937; yearbook: Echo/Legacy). After the 1971 move the original building became Holman Junior High/Middle School; its 'A Complex' was torn down May 1988. The 1971 site was in the village of Champ, annexed into Maryland Heights in December 1994 - actual ZIP is 63043, not the seed's 63044. DATA-QUALITY FLAG: same continuous school as ALL-148 'Pattonville High School' and ALL-149 'Pattonville High School - Original Campus' in other batches (see schools_seed_deduped_review_needed.json); kept separate per batch structure - for yearbook purposes this is one yearbook series spanning both campuses.

name: St. Charles Rock Road School
notes: UNRESOLVED IDENTITY: no school literally named 'St. Charles Rock Road School' appears in Pattonville's published district history or elsewhere; the name reads like a road-address label lifted from a directory/record. Two plausible referents: (a) Junction School, the one-room school at the St. Charles Rock Road/Natural Bridge intersection (opened 1869, merged with Penn School in 1936 to form Penn-Junction; site is now SSM DePaul Hospital) - the best geographic match for a school known by its St. Charles Rock Road location; (b) the original Pattonville High School building at 11055 St. Charles Rock Road (occupied 1936-1971, then Holman Middle School; 'A Complex' demolished 1988). Wikipedia's Pattonville article also notes 'Penn Elementary School (a one-room school), located on Old St Charles Rock Rd... closed in the 1940s' - a third possible referent. Left unresolved rather than guessed; a human could resolve this by finding the source record the seed compiler used.

name: Bridgeton Senior High School
historical_names: Bridgeton High School
notes: LIKELY PHANTOM: no evidence a public 'Bridgeton (Senior) High School' ever operated in Bridgeton, MO - searches surface only Bridgeton High School in Bridgeton, New Jersey. The Bridgeton School District itself was real (incorporated by the legislature in 1864, covering Bridgeton and Bridgeton Commons; its town school was the Moravian School/Bridgeton Academy, an elementary-level institution still standing as late as 1968). Like the other small north-county districts, it appears to have sent students to neighboring high schools on tuition rather than operating its own (Pattonville students went to Ritenour, Normandy and University City until Pattonville HS opened in 1936; the same pattern applied to Bridgeton). The district was annexed into Pattonville during the 1949-1950 school year, which matches the seed's 'Closed: 1950'. If this row intends the Bridgeton district's secondary students, their effective destination was Pattonville High School (ALL-198) - recorded as probable context, not a confirmed successor, since the existence of the school itself is unverified. Retained per no-silent-delete rule.

name: Airport Elementary School
historical_names: Airport School
district_operator: Ferguson-Florissant School District (Berkeley School District before 1975)
notes: SEED ATTRIBUTION WRONG - CORRECTED: the only 'Airport Elementary School' in north St. Louis County is at 8249 Airport Road, Berkeley MO 63134 (city documents also use 8429 Airport Rd) - a Ferguson-Florissant R-II school, not Pattonville R-III, and in Berkeley rather than the seed's 'Bridgeton/Earth City' (it is ~3 miles southeast of Bridgeton). School and gymnasium built in 1954 (City of Berkeley RFP; corroborated by the 1984 appellate decision Szombathy v. Ferguson-Florissant R-2 describing the 1954 construction). Closed at the end of the 2018-19 school year under the FFSD redistricting plan (Berkeley residents sued to keep it open); the City of Berkeley purchased the property in 2023 for conversion to a community center. No successor school - students were redistributed within FFSD. DATA-QUALITY FLAG: likely the same school as ALL-390 'Airport Elementary School - Historical Campus' in another batch (flagged pair in schools_seed_deduped_review_needed.json) - coordinate with that batch's output rather than double-recording.

name: Old Elm Grove School
historical_names: Elm Grove School; Elm Grove School District No. 9; Little Red Schoolhouse
district_operator: Elm Grove District No. 9; Hazelwood School District (after ~1952)
notes: Confirmed by the City of Hazelwood historical marker (via HMDB): built 1852, one of the earliest school buildings in St. Louis County; closed in 1952 following the organization of the Hazelwood School District; moved to Brookes Park and rebuilt to its 1890s appearance; federal historic listing June 14, 1970. Esley Hamilton's 'Surviving Rural Schools in St. Louis County' (St. Louis Architecture newsletter, Spring 2013) records it as 'Elm Grove School #9, 450 Brookes Dr., Hazelwood - district established 1852, brick building later'. DISCREPANCY: marker and seed say the building was moved in 1966; the Hamilton inventory and flovalleynews.com say 1961 - the move year does not affect the school's operating dates. The specific Hazelwood elementary that absorbed its students is not documented online (successor unknown). DATA-QUALITY FLAG: near-certain duplicate of ALL-027 'Elm Grove School' in another batch (flagged pair in schools_seed_deduped_review_needed.json) - same school, coordinate outputs.

name: Melrose School #57
historical_names: Melrose School; Melrose School District No. 57
district_operator: Melrose District No. 57 (rural district; later merged into a west-county district)
notes: SEED LOCATION WRONG - CORRECTED: the seed assigns this to the 'Hazelwood predecessor' district at '18820 Melrose Road Florissant MO 63031', but 18820 Melrose Road is in Wildwood (ZIP 63038, Ward Six) in far-west St. Louis County, in the historic Village of Melrose (platted 1851 by Charles H. Haven) - roughly 25 miles from Hazelwood and outside the RECA ZIPs this seed row claims to serve. Esley Hamilton's county-wide inventory ('Surviving Rural Schools in St. Louis County', St. Louis Architecture newsletter, Spring 2013, based on the county's 1991 rural-schools inventory) lists 'Melrose School #57, 18820 Melrose Rd., circa 1859, now a residence' - matching the seed's c.1859 opening. The Wildwood Historical Society holds 1931/1937 photos of the school, and the City of Wildwood's Historic Preservation Commission considered acquiring 'the Old Melrose School, 18820 Melrose Road' in Jan 2019. Exact closure year not found: as a numbered rural district (#57 in the county's 1910 renumbering), it almost certainly closed when Missouri merged the rural districts into modern districts between 1947 and 1954 - consistent with the seed's '1950s' - but no specific date or successor school is documented online. Recommended human follow-up: the Wildwood Historical Society holds records/photos that could pin down the closing date and receiving district (likely an ancestor of Rockwood or Eureka).

name: Buder Elementary School
historical_names: Buder School
notes: Per Ritenour's '100 Interesting Ritenour Facts': Buder School opened September 1939 north and east of the Ashby School site, replacing the Ashby School portable (grades 1-4, 1936-1939 at Ashby Road & Clarendon Ave). Named for Hugo F. Buder, board member 1932-1939 who as board president obtained the property. Interrupted operation: closed 1981 due to declining enrollment and reopened 1986. Currently operating as Buder Elementary, 10350 Baltimore Ave, St. Ann (Ritenour's website and NCES). Seed's 'Unknown' opening resolved.

name: Hoech Middle School
historical_names: Hoech Junior High School; Hoech School
notes: Per Ritenour's '100 Interesting Ritenour Facts': the property at 3312 Ashby Road was obtained in 1952 for $100, and a 1953 bond issue funded construction of Hoech Junior High School, which opened mid-year in January 1955. Named for Arthur A. Hoech, Ritenour's longest-serving superintendent (1920-1956). Now operating as Hoech Middle School (junior-high-to-middle conversion year not found online; Ritenour currently lists it as a middle school). Seed's 'Unknown' opening resolved.

name: Robert Drummond Elementary School
historical_names: Drummond Elementary School
notes: Seed confirmed: opened August 2002 (dedicated Aug 29, 2002), built with Lambert St. Louis International Airport funds as the joint replacement for Carrollton Elementary (ALL-180) and Carrollton Oaks Elementary (ALL-179, other batch), both demolished for the runway expansion. Pattonville bought 17 acres at the site of Hope Lutheran School (itself the former St. Ann Elementary, closed effective the 1982-83 school year) at 3721 St. Bridget Lane, St. Ann - hence the same address as the former St. Ann Elementary. Named for Robert Drummond, Pattonville board member 1972-2002. First principal Jim Schwab had been principal of Carrollton Oaks. Currently operating (drummond.psdr3.org).

name: Pattonville Early Childhood Center
historical_names: Pattonville Preschool; Early Childhood Center; Briar Crest Elementary School (same building, 1965-2013)
notes: Seed confirmed: opened August 2018 (2018-19 school year) at 2900 Adie Road, St. Ann - the former Briar Crest Elementary School building (opened 1965, closed 2013 for budget cuts, leased to a private school/YWCA in the interim), renovated with a 2017 no-tax-rate-increase bond. Houses Pattonville's preschool (ages 3-5) and Parents as Teachers programs; the district's early childhood program itself was created August 2002 and was previously scattered across elementary schools and the Pattonville Learning Center (1995-2018). Currently operating (earlychildhood.psdr3.org). NOTE for yearbook purposes: an early-childhood center almost certainly publishes no yearbook; the underlying building's Briar Crest Elementary era (1965-2013) is the yearbook-relevant lineage if a Briar Crest row exists elsewhere in the dataset.

name: Ritenour High School
historical_names: Ritenour Senior High School
notes: Continuous high-school entity: first four-year program enrolled ten freshmen in fall 1914 (classes in the Ritenour/Overland grade-school building, now ALL-304); first graduating class May 17, 1918. Dedicated building opened September 1924 on Forest Avenue (ALL-303); moved to the current 9100 St. Charles Rock Road campus for the 1950-51 term (21.5-acre site purchased 1935; $630K bond approved December 1946; Class of 1951 first to graduate there). Seed's '1927' is unverified and likely conflates a later milestone; Wikipedia lists 'Established 1911' based on earlier HS-level coursework (first-year-equivalent studies began 1910 per State ex rel. Bender v. Hackmann, Mo. 1922). School still operating. Physical ZIP is 63114 (Breckenridge Hills); seed's 63074 reflects served community.

name: Ritenour Middle School
historical_names: Ritenour Junior High; Ritenour Junior High School
notes: Occupies the original 1924 Ritenour High School building (8740 Forest Ave; same site as ALL-303). Became the district's first junior high when the new high school opened for the 1950-51 term — the district hired James A. Painter as its first junior-high principal in May 1950 in anticipation. Became a middle school in 1981 when sixth graders moved up from elementaries and ninth graders moved to the high school. The 1923-built portion was demolished in 1991 and replaced. Still operating. Seed ZIP 63074 is served-community; physical address 2500 Marshall Ave is 63114.

name: DeHart School
historical_names: Lewis DeHart School; Lewis DeHart Eight Room Elementary School
notes: Land at St. Charles Rock Road & Wismer Avenue (Breckenridge Hills) offered by the DeHart sisters in November 1943 and purchased early 1944 ($1,000-$2,600 across three deeds) with reverter conditions requiring a school for white children named the 'Lewis DeHart School,' honoring their father, a Ritenour board member/president 1889-1900. Building bid ($97,685) accepted August 1944; completed 1945. Closed after the 1979-80 year per the district's own history ('closed in 1980'); the 1983 Missouri Court of Appeals opinion in DeHart v. Ritenour Consolidated School District (663 S.W.2d 332) records classes 'from 1945 until 1981' — a one-year discrepancy, likely school-year vs. record-year. Property sold 1988; demolished for Centennial Bank, which holds a memorial plaque (dedicated September 8, 1988) and a cornerstone time capsule was recovered. Receiving school not identified. Seed ZIP 63074 is served-community; physical location is Breckenridge Hills, 63114.

name: Iveland Elementary School
historical_names: Iveland School
notes: Resolved seed's '1940s': the school's own history page records a four-acre site bought with February 1928 bond funds ($8,000) and a permanent one-story four-room building built in 1936 (a WPA-era project per the district history; sight-saving classes had run in a portable on the site from 1935). Principal Lillian Kegelman served 1936-1969. Additions 1949, 1956, 1964, and post-1990 rebuild. Still operating at 1836 Dyer Ave. Seed ZIP 63074 is served-community; physical ZIP is 63114 (Overland).

name: Buck School
historical_names: Buck Schoolhouse
notes: One-room log cabin built 1846 near Woodson and Lackland roads on land donated by Elizabeth Smith; first teacher Thomas W. Goldie at $20/month. In 1867 it joined a nearby temporary school for Negro children to form the rural Ritenour district and took the name Ritenour School — that is the 'closed' date, an identity change rather than a shutdown (district states the lineage explicitly: Buck School -> Ritenour School -> Overland School -> Old Overland School -> Administrative Center; successor row ALL-321 'Ritenour School' lives in another batch). The original log building was destroyed by fire December 28, 1886 (board minutes attribute it to a flue defect, not the often-retold Christmas-tree myth) and was replaced by a two-room brick building completed summer 1887 for $2,245. Seed's 'closed unknown' resolved.

name: Lackland Avenue School
historical_names: Lackland School; Lackland Avenue School for Negro children
notes: Frame 16'x24' schoolhouse on Lackland Avenue (at Sims Avenue, Overland) built on land purchased August 1888 ($2,000); opened the second Monday in October 1888 as the district's school for Negro children. On August 12, 1913 the board designated it the site of a high-school class for Negro students — the first for African-American pupils in St. Louis County. The board voted shortly before the end of 1915 to close it and consolidate operations with the new Elmwood building (ALL-292); the building was sold June 1917 for $65. Seed's '1900s' opening corrected to 1888; seed's 1915 close and the Lackland->Elmwood merge both confirmed by the district's commissioned history and its 100 Facts page.

name: Elmwood Park School
historical_names: Elmwood School
notes: District's school for African-American children in the Elmwood Park subdivision (Chicago Heights Blvd & Dielman Rd). Began as a rented 'branch school' whose classes started December 4, 1899 (Block 9, Robertson Street); later housed in the Elmwood Park Baptist Church (through May 1912) and the rented 'Fisher place' before the permanent building — funded by the April 15, 1915 bond issue (227-108) — was built starting June 1915 and absorbed the Lackland Avenue School that year. Remained an all-Black school even after district-wide integration began in 1958; an HEW directive forced a plan (implemented ~1974-75) that divided Elmwood students among Wyland, New Overland (ALL-308, another batch) and Iveland (ALL-289) schools and moved the Vo-Prep program into the Elmwood building. 'Closed' recorded as 1975 (last classes under that dispersal; the district history says both the Elmwood building and the original Vo-Prep building were sold in summer 1976 — exact final year could be 1975 or 1976). Seed's '1900s' open and 'unknown' close both resolved. No single successor — students were dispersed per the HEW plan.

name: Holy Trinity School
historical_names: Holy Trinity Parish School
district_operator: Holy Trinity Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: SEED ERROR: 'Closed 2024' is actually the date Ritenour School District purchased the property (closed August 13/20, 2024, $1 million, for its Center for Educational Excellence) — the school itself closed at the end of the 2018-19 year (127 students, enrollment down 67% since 2002), per the St. Louis Review; the Archdiocese announcement is dated April 2019. Holy Trinity School was itself established in 2002 as a consolidation of St. William, St. Kevin, St. Gregory and All Souls parish schools (opened K-8 with 382 students), occupying the former St. Kevin School building at 10901 St. Henry Lane; it also absorbed Our Lady of the Presentation (Overland) students when that school closed in 2009. Parish itself closed June 2020. No successor school — students dispersed. For pre-2002 coverage of this site, the predecessor parish schools (St. Kevin, St. Gregory, St. William, All Souls) deserve their own rows if not already batched.

name: Hope Lutheran School - St. Ann
historical_names: Hope Lutheran School; Hope Lutheran School-St Ann
notes: SEED CORRECTION: seed status 'Current/Unknown' is stale — privateschoolreview lists the school as 'Closed 2016' after continuous operation since 1943 (its own profile text; a directory listing also says 'Since 1943'). The sponsoring congregation, Hope Lutheran Church (joined LCMS December 31, 1945 per the LCMS church locator; IRS exemption July 1941), remains active at 10701 St. Cosmas Lane. Single aggregating source for both dates — mark probable and corroborate via MO DESE nonpublic records or Missouri District LCMS reports if precision matters.

name: American Trade School
historical_names: American Trade School
notes: For-profit HVAC/electrical trade school at 3925 Industrial Drive; BBB records business start July 1, 2003 and incorporation July 25, 2003, consistent with LinkedIn and tradeschoolsreview 'founded 2003.' ACCSC-accredited. Still operating. As the seed notes, unlikely to produce traditional yearbooks — low value for the archive survey.

name: Olivet University - St. Louis Campus
historical_names: Olivet University St. Louis; St. Ann Campus
notes: Olivet University (evangelical institution founded as Olivet Theological College & Seminary in 2000, incorporated as a university 2004 in California) established its St. Ann campus at 10257 St. Charles Rock Road circa 2023 — a City of St. Ann special-use permit for 'a Bible College' at the address (property owner Jonathan Park) was heard April 24, 2023, noting the site was 'Formerly Brookes Bible College.' Olivet now lists St. Ann as its MAIN campus and held its first Missouri convocation there in September 2026. The building itself opened May 2014 as Brookes Bible College (a separate, now-closed institution worth its own seed row if not already covered). Olivet had a St. Louis extension site by the late 2010s per Wikipedia. Low yearbook value.

name: St. Ann School District
historical_names: Historical St. Ann public school district
notes: LIKELY PHANTOM DISTRICT: found no evidence an independent 'St. Ann School District' ever existed. The city of St. Ann was platted by developer Charles Vatterott beginning 1943 and incorporated in 1948 — recent enough that it never formed its own district; it has always been served by the Ritenour School District (which covered much of the area since 1867 and annexed Scudder District territory in 1940 and 1949) and the Pattonville R-3 district. Schools physically in St. Ann included Pattonville's St. Ann Elementary (seed row ALL-174, another batch), Ritenour's DeHart and Iveland elementaries, and the parochial schools. A 1943 Vatterott letter to the Ritenour board proposing a 'St. Ann's Public School' shows Ritenour already being treated as the area's district before the city existed. Recommend retaining only as a search alias; a human could confirm via DESE historical district directories or St. Louis County recorder records that no St. Ann district was ever organized.

name: Ritenour Consolidated School District
historical_names: Ritenour Consolidated District; Ritenour School District; Ritenour District (rural district, 1867); Ritenour Village School District (1907)
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT — no yearbook of its own; Track B should target member schools. Timeline (district's commissioned history 'Ritenour: Our First 132 Years' + Missouri Supreme Court in State ex rel. Bender v. Hackmann, 1922, and MoHistory's 1926 commencement-program record, which both style it 'Ritenour Consolidated School District'): rural district formed 1867 by joining Buck School and a temporary Negro school (named for landowner J.S. Ritenour); reorganized as a village district with a six-member board April 1907; 'Consolidated' in use by 1921-22 litigation — seed's 'organized as a consolidated district in 1910' is unverified and likely conflates 1910, the year the district began first-year high-school coursework per the court opinion. Seed's note that land was added from the Scudder District in 1940 and 1949 is corroborated by the district history. Member schools include, in this batch: Ritenour HS (ALL-285), Ritenour Middle/Junior High (ALL-287), DeHart (ALL-288), Iveland (ALL-289), Lackland (ALL-291), Elmwood (ALL-292); in other batches: Ritenour School (ALL-321), Overland School (ALL-309), New Overland (ALL-308), Scudder Avenue School (ALL-392); plus unbatched/unnamed: Home Heights, Midland, Marion, Marvin, Kratz, Wyland, Buder, Ashby, Hoech Junior High, Ritenour School for Early Childhood Education. Still operating; NCES District ID 1931680.

name: Ritenour High School - Forest Avenue Campus
historical_names: Ritenour High School; Ritenour Senior High School (Forest Ave building)
notes: Ritenour's first dedicated high-school building at 8740 Forest Avenue (Charlack site — parts of Blocks 35-36 purchased March 1921 from Edward Gocke; $65K bond approved May 1921, re-approved October 1921, bonds sold March 1923, cornerstone laid July 1923, designed with input from William B. Ittner's firm). Opened September 1924 for the 1924-25 year; served as the senior high until the new St. Charles Rock Road campus (ALL-285) opened for the 1950-51 term, then became the district's first junior high — the same building is today's Ritenour Middle School (ALL-287) at 2500 Marshall Ave. The 1923-built portion was demolished in 1991. Kept as a separate row per the no-silent-merge campus rule.

name: Ritenour High School - Old Overland Campus
historical_names: Overland School; Ritenour/Overland School; Ritenour School (1907 building)
notes: High-school program housed inside the district's main grade school at 2420 Woodson Road — the 1907 eight-room building erected on the site of the earlier Ritenour School (Buck School site; the building is separately seeded as ALL-309 'Overland School'). The Missouri Supreme Court in State ex rel. Bender v. Hackmann (1922) records that the 1907 building, erected for grade-school purposes, began housing 'first-year high-school course' studies in 1910, added second-year studies 1914 and third/fourth-year by 1916 — seed's '1918' conflates the first graduating class (May 17, 1918). The high school moved to the new Forest Avenue building (ALL-303) in September 1924. The Woodson Road building continued as the Overland/New Overland elementary and is today the district Administrative Center.

name: Marion Elementary School
historical_names: Marion School
notes: Seed's 1925 confirmed by the district's own history page: a $70,000 bond issue passed in January 1925 to build Marion (paired with Midland), and 'the school opened in 1925.' Site land at Midland & Marion (now Sims Avenue) was acquired in stages in 1888, 1918 and 1923. Additions/renovations in 1953 and 1959; the 1990 bond issue funded demolition of the old building and replacement with the current $2,625,700 structure (consistent with the seed note); library renovation completed 2012 under Prop K. School site is live and the building is a current Ritenour elementary.

name: New Overland School
historical_names: New Overland Elementary School
notes: Seed's 1929 confirmed: district history page says the school was 'built in 1929 on Woodson Road in Overland' after land was assembled from ten owners; a $69,000 bond issue for it passed 277-30 on Feb. 12, 1929 (per the district's 'Our First 132 Years' history). CLOSURE-YEAR CONFLICT: the district's 100-facts page says it closed in 1975 (matching the seed), but the district's own narrative history says the March 25, 1976 reorganization plan designated Home Heights, Midland and New Overland 'to be closed,' the Armbruster Vo-Prep School moved into the New Overland building in summer 1976, and Elmwood students were still being reassigned TO New Overland for 1975-76 when Elmwood closed — implying the elementary program actually ended in 1976. Recorded 1976 as the better-evidenced year; 1975 is possible if the district's fact list refers to the program wind-down. Receiving elementaries for displaced students are not named in either source. The building was sold to the U.S. Postal Service in 1997 and demolished; the site is now the Overland Post Office (district fact 35) — consistent with the seed note.

name: Overland School
historical_names: Ritenour/Overland School; Ritenour School; Old Overland School
notes: SEED CLOSURE YEAR WRONG: seed says closed 1924, but the building at 2420 Woodson Rd operated as a school until 1958. District history: in April 1907 the board hired an architect to plan a new eight-room building on the Ritenour School site, and 'Ritenour' opened on time that fall. The district's fact 14 summarizes the site lineage — 'from 1847 to 1958, the location of the Administrative Center was the site of a school — first the Buck School, which became the Ritenour School, which later became the Overland School, which later became the Old Overland School.' Wyland Elementary opened September 1958 and 'replaced' the old Overland School (narrative: 'the board made plans to sell the old Overland School, which it replaced'); no buyer emerged and the building was remodeled into the Ritenour Administrative Center, which still stands at 2420 Woodson Rd. The seed's 1924 is probably the year the district's high-school classes moved out — the new Ritenour High School opened its own building in fall 1924 (that building is today's Ritenour Middle School, district fact 17). The Overland School building had housed Ritenour's early high school classes since 1914. SUCCESSOR GAP: Wyland Elementary School (opened 1958, still operating) is the documented replacement but has NO row anywhere in the seed dataset — recommend adding it. LINEAGE FLAG: this row is the same continuous school as ALL-321 'Ritenour School' (1867-1907 in the seed); they are name/building phases of one entity, kept separate per the no-silent-merge rule.

name: Home Heights School
historical_names: Home Heights School
notes: Seed confirmed on both dates by the district's own history: a $2,000 bond for a 'wooden school' in the Home Heights/St. John area was approved April 1905 and 'the first Home Heights School building opened in 1907' (narrative adds the fall 1907 opening was delayed a month). The four-room brick replacement was approved May 1915 and opened Jan. 31, 1916 (narrative gives the exact opening date and a Feb. 5 open house). A $60,000 WPA-assisted addition passed in November 1933. 'Home Heights School closed in 1976' under the March 25, 1976 board reorganization plan; the building then housed the district's expanded Community Education Program before being 'demolished in 1998 to develop an outstanding soccer facility on the site, now known as the Ritenour High School North Campus Athletic Field.' Receiving school(s) for its students were not specified in the district sources — left successor unknown. Color detail: Charles Lindbergh photographed the school from the air on Oct. 2, 1926.

name: Midland School
historical_names: Midland Elementary School
notes: Seed confirmed on both dates by the district's history: the Midland site next to the original high school off Forest Avenue in Charlack 'was obtained in 1923 for $1. It was built in 1925 and closed in 1976. The school was demolished in 1991, with most of the site to be used by Ritenour Middle School for playground and recreational purposes.' Architect plans for Marion and Midland were commissioned September 1924 and the paired $70,000 bond passed Jan. 20, 1925 (narrative history). After closure the building was leased to the Special School District (summer 1976) before its 1991 demolition. Receiving elementary school(s) for its students are not documented in the district sources — successor left unknown. (Seed 'demolished 1991' confirmed.)

name: Marvin Elementary School
historical_names: Marvin School
notes: Seed's 1928 confirmed by the district's history: the school 'derived its name from the Marvin Park subdivision,' a February 1928 bond issue funded the site purchase, and 'it opened in 1928 with six teachers and 302 pupils.' A $37,000 addition bond passed Feb. 11, 1930; the site grew to ~10 acres (1956-67); the 1990 bond issue replaced the older portions with the current 1991 building ($3,102,000); a second gym was completed for the 2006 school year. School website is live — still a current Ritenour elementary.

name: Ashby School
historical_names: Ashby Road School
notes: OPENING-YEAR CONFLICT: seed says 1936, and the district's own fact list says the portable 'housed grades 1-4 from 1936 to 1939' — but the district's narrative history says the portable (purchased 1922 for the Overland School site) 'was moved to a new location on Ashby Road' in September 1933 to temporarily meet the need for a school. The 1933 date is from board-minutes-derived narrative; 1936 may reflect when it first appears in the district's grade-level listings. Recorded 1933 probable with the conflict documented. CLOSURE CONFIRMED: the $39,073 contract for a permanent Ashby School was let in November 1938; the new building opened in September 1939 as Buder School (renamed for board president Hugo F. Buder, who died March 1939) 'north and east of the Ashby School,' and the portable was sold to St. Luke's AME Church in Elmwood for $400. Successor recorded as ALL-314 (Buder Elementary, the 63114 row) per the district's explicit 'replaced by Buder School.' NOTE: ALL-314's own seed row says Buder closed 1981 — Buder did close 1981 but reopened in 1986 and is operating today (district fact list); flag for that batch's worker. Buder also appears as ALL-261 in the 63074 rows — likely a duplicate of the same school.

name: Ritenour School
historical_names: Ritenour School; Ritenour/Overland School; Buck School (predecessor, 1846)
notes: Seed note corroborated: in 1867 'Buck School and a temporary school for Negro children were joined to form the rural district of Ritenour' (district history PDF), making Ritenour the first St. Louis-area district to educate African-American children. The name honored landowner J.S. Ritenour (d. March 29, 1867). The school itself is older than the name — Buck School was a one-room log cabin built 1846 at Woodson/Lackland (site of today's Administrative Center); it burned Dec. 28, 1886 (flue defect, not the Christmas-tree legend) and was replaced by a four-room brick building. 'Ritenour School' in this seed row (1867-1907) is the same continuous school as ALL-309 'Overland School' — the 1907 date marks the eight-room replacement building on the same site, not a true closure, and board minutes keep calling the school 'Ritenour' well into the 1910s before 'Overland'/'Old Overland' usage takes over. Successor = ALL-309 (the same entity continued under the Overland School name until 1958). LINEAGE FLAG: rows ALL-321 and ALL-309 describe one school; kept separate per the no-silent-merge rule.

name: Normandy High School
historical_names: Normandy Senior High School
notes: Seed's '1920s' resolved: the school's own site says it 'opened its doors for the 1923-24 school year' — voters approved a $200,000 bond in April 1924 (authorized 1922 per the State Historical Society of Missouri's S0326 finding aid) to buy the former Eden Seminary campus at Lucas & Hunt Rd / St. Charles Rock Rd, and the school shared the campus with the seminary during 1923-24 (~300 students, 13 teachers). It opened as a combined junior/senior high (grades 7-12); William B. Ittner designed the California-style campus, a vocational building and amphitheater gym were added 1929, a junior-high building was added on campus 1934, and a separate junior high opened ~1949 after a fire gutted the original seminary building. Still operating under Normandy Schools Collaborative (the district formed July 12, 1894; renamed/reorganized after losing accreditation in 2013-14). Actual address ZIP is 63133 (Wellston), not 63114 — included for community coverage. The seed's yearbook list (1931, 1933, 1935, etc.) is plausible; see ALL-329 for the pre-1923 predecessor high school.

name: Normandy High School - Historical Campus
historical_names: Normandy High School (Washington School campus)
notes: Interpreting this row as the pre-1923 Normandy high school (the seed asks to keep it separate because 'campus and institutional names changed'). The SHSMO Normandy School District Collection says the district's first high school classes were taught in 1907 in the old Washington School building on St. Charles Rock Road; the first class (4 students) graduated in 1911, and the high school 'could not meet accreditation requirements and was closed in the spring of 1912.' (Wikipedia says 'only one class graduated when the school closed in 1911' — one-year conflict noted; used 1912 from the archival finding aid.) Wikipedia also notes an even earlier, undated, sub-one-year high-school attempt at Lincoln Elementary in Pagedale. No high school existed in Normandy 1912-1923 — students attended neighboring districts' schools — until the Eden Seminary campus opened as ALL-328 in 1923, recorded as successor (the institutional continuation, though not a direct merger). LINEAGE FLAG: this is a predecessor-phase row for ALL-328, not a separate institution.

name: Normandy Junior High School

district_operator: Normandy School District / Normandy Schools Collaborative
notes: Junior-high instruction in Normandy began inside the high school — NHS opened as a combined junior/senior high in 1923, and a junior-high building was added to the high-school campus in 1934 (SHSMO S0326). As a standalone school, the district bought a 30-acre Natural Bridge Road tract from the Sisters of the Cenacle in 1947, began construction in 1948, and the separate junior high opened ~1949 (Wikipedia's building-year list gives 'Normandy Junior High School - 1949'; the school's 'NorJun' newsletter exists for 1960-61 in the SHSMO collection). The same Wikipedia list notes the school later operated as 'Normandy Junior High/Middle (and later 7th-8th Grade Center).' The 'Normandy Junior High' name/building's exact end date is not pinned down online: NSC's current middle school is Normandy Middle School at Lucas Crossing (7837 Natural Bridge Rd; Lucas Crossing complex built 2004 per its school page, which cites the site as the former district administration/Lucas-Hunt property), and NSC reconfigured to a grades 1-8 'EleMiddle' model in 2019-20 (normandysc.org). The NSC Early Learning Center at 7855 Natural Bridge Rd may occupy the old junior-high site — plausible but unverified. Successor recorded as ALL-343 (Normandy Middle School at Lucas Crossing) as the functional continuation of the district's middle grades; interestingly that row's own seed 'Opened' value is 1949, suggesting the seed already treats it as the NJH continuation.

CLOSED AND REOPENED: the board voted Oct. 24, 2013 to close Bel-Nor amid the district's financial collapse; its ~332 students left on Dec. 20, 2013 and were folded into two other Normandy elementaries (AP/St. Louis Post-Dispatch via tucson.com; Wikipedia records the closure as 2014). A 2015 plan repurposed the building for kindergarten, and the school is active again — the NSC site lists it as the district's only grades 1-5 school with ~300 students. Recorded closed_year n/a since it operates today, with the 2013-14 closure documented here. During the closure its students dispersed to other district elementaries, so successor is 'none' for the reopened entity. Actual address ZIP is 63121 (Bel-Nor).

Recorded 2011 probable. Which elementaries absorbed its students is not documented — successor unknown. The Missouri Historical Society genealogy photo index holds a 'Bel-Ridge Primary School' image, consistent with an early-grades configuration.

Per a St. Louis Post-Dispatch article quoted by UrbanReview STL, the building 'opened in 1907 as the Loretto Academy, a posh school for girls'; Nerinx Hall's own LibGuide dates 'Loretto Academy (St. Louis, MO)' as closed 1952, when the school moved to/merged with Nerinx Hall High School in Webster Groves (successor, no seed row). Nothing ties a 'Loretto Academy' to ZIP 63114 (Overland/St. Ann/Breckenridge Hills); the Sisters of Loretto school actually in that area was St. Ann parish school in Normandy, a different entity. name: Normandy High School - Eden Seminary Campus

Wikipedia's NSC school list gives 'Normandy High School - 1925'; opening year given as 1923 here (first year of operation). A 1949 fire burned most of the ornate four-story seminary building; classes ran split-session 1949-50; the surviving first floor was demolished in 1958 and replaced by Central Hall (completed ~1959). 'Closed 1958' therefore refers only to the original building. The continuing school is tracked separately in batch10 (ALL-328 'Normandy High School'; ALL-329 'Normandy High School - Historical Campus' is probably this same campus) -- flagged as cross-batch overlap, not merged. Actual ZIP is 63133 (Wellston), not 63121.

notes: Confirmed operating: NCES lists Bermuda Elementary, 5835 Bermuda Dr, St. Louis 63121 (in Normandy), currently a PK-2 'Bermuda Primary School' under FFSD's grade-band reconfiguration. SEED ADDRESS ERROR: '11600 Old Halls Ferry Road?' is wrong — that corridor is in Jennings/North County; the school is at 5835 Bermuda Dr. Opening year not found — publicschoolreview's enrollment series begins 1989 (the school clearly predates it; likely post-war suburban construction but no dated source surfaced), and hubbiz's 'established 1997' is unreliable. Recommend human follow-up in FFSD facility records or Normandy Area Historical Association/SHSMO materials for a build date.

name: University City High School
historical_names: University City High School; U City High School
notes: Seed's '1920s' refined: the Art Deco building at 7401 Balson Ave was designed in 1928 by Trueblood & Graf and opened in 1930 (district's own history page; NRHP nomination for the University City Education District, listed 1985). The institution likely predates the building — the School District of University City was formally established February 1911 and ran earlier secondary grades — so 1930 is the building/campus opening. Still operating. SEED ZIP NOTE: the school is actually in University City, ZIP 63130; included in this batch because pre-1922 Normandy students attended surrounding districts' high schools before Normandy had an accredited high school (SHSMO S0326; Kinloch HS article similarly notes white Kinloch-area students attended Normandy/Ritenour/Ferguson high schools). Relevant as a pre-1922 (and later tuition/transfer) search target for Normandy-area claimants.

name: Normandy Area Historical Association
historical_names: Normandy Area Historical Association; NAHA
notes: DATA-QUALITY FLAG — NOT A SCHOOL: NAHA is the key Normandy-area historical society, established as a nonprofit in 1974 (Missouri Historical Society ArchivesSpace biographical note) after forming to save the Clark 'Minoma' house; it instead preserved the Hunt House/Shelter/Cenacle at 7717 Natural Bridge Rd as its longtime home. It documented the history of ~20 North County municipalities for over 30 years; its collections are now at the Missouri Historical Society (NAHA Collection — incl. 'Normandy School District History, presented by Fred Small, 1991') and SHSMO (S0420, records 1877-2008, incl. photographs and yearbooks per SHSMO's description — matching the seed's claim that it holds Normandy High yearbooks). No evidence found that it still operates as an active organization — the archival deposits suggest it is inactive or dissolved, date unfound. RECOMMENDATION: exclude from the schools table and carry it as an archive/holdings lead for Track B work (both its MoHistory and SHSMO deposits are directly relevant to the yearbook survey). entity_type set to ambiguous_unresolved only because the enum lacks a 'not_a_school' value.

name: Berkeley High School - Hancock Campus
historical_names: Hancock School; The Little Red Schoolhouse; Kinloch High School (white campus); Kinloch School
district_operator: Kinloch School District / Berkeley School District
notes: Campus-level row for Berkeley High School's original home at 5924 Hancock Ave, the 'Little Red Schoolhouse' — the building itself is much older than the seed's 1937: it was built in 1902-03 (cornerstone August 1902) as the Kinloch School District No. 5 school for white students, and it housed both elementary AND high-school classes by 1932-1935 (City of Berkeley history page; alumni reunion site). The 1937 date marks the Berkeley identity: the Berkeley School District formed in 1937 amid a segregation dispute (white residents drew the new City of Berkeley's boundaries to exclude Black families), and the district's 'white' Kinloch high school was renamed Berkeley High School (Wikipedia, Berkeley, MO + Kinloch HS articles). END OF HS USE AT HANCOCK UNRESOLVED — deliberately left 'unknown' rather than accepting the seed's 1947: the alumni site is titled 'BHS Reunion 1938-1960', which brackets the Hancock-era HS classes through ~1960 and conflicts with 1947; Wikipedia confirms 'a new Berkeley High School campus opened in a new location' at some later point but gives no date. The building continued as an elementary school afterward (survived the 2011 Good Friday tornado). Successor is the continuing institution Berkeley High School (dataset row ALL-114 — other campus rows ALL-380 Caroline Ave, ALL-381 Walter Ave are in other batches); the institution closed December 2003 (Lambert airport expansion) and was replaced by McCluer South-Berkeley HS (opened January 2004).

name: Berkeley High School - Caroline Avenue Campus
historical_names: Berkeley High School; Berkeley Junior High School (building reuse)
notes: Second Berkeley High School campus at 6033 Caroline Ave per the seed. The seed's 1947-1955 window is plausible but not independently pinned down: the BHS alumni reunion site shows the high school 'brand new in 1937' (likely the ALL-379 Hancock building) and a 'Berkeley Junior and Senior High School' photo dated c.1954, and a St. Louis Post-Dispatch school listing (newspapers.com page 139531531) shows 'BERKELEY JUNIOR HIGH 6033 Caroline' while the senior high was at '8710 Walter' — consistent with Caroline serving as the high school until the Walter Ave building opened ~1955, then being reused as Berkeley Junior High and later the 'Caroline Support Center' (56housesleft.com documents it in the airport buyout zone). Possibility not ruled out: the Caroline building itself dates to 1937 (the WPA-funded 'white' high school), which would make the seed's 1947 wrong — unresolved either way. Berkeley alumni report three school buildings were demolished for Lambert airport expansion (the 1937-era high school building, an elementary school, and the newer high school); the Caroline building is likely among them. High-school function moved to the Walter Avenue campus (ALL-381).

name: Berkeley High School - Walter Avenue Campus
historical_names: Berkeley High School; Berkeley Senior High School
notes: Final Berkeley High School campus at 8710 Walter Ave (a 1992 DOE FUSRAP public-meeting notice confirms the school at this address; schools-us.org directory also lists 'Berkeley Senior High, 8710 Walter Avenue'). Opened ~1955 per seed; an airport-buyout-era inventory (56housesleft.com) described the building as 'over 40 years' old in 1998, consistent with a mid-1950s construction. The Berkeley district was court-annexed into Ferguson-Florissant on June 7, 1975 (US v. State of Missouri, 388 F. Supp. 1058; affirmed 515 F.2d 1365). Classes ended in December 2003 due to Lambert-St. Louis Airport expansion and the school is conventionally listed as closed 2004; students moved to the newly opened McCluer South-Berkeley High School (ALL-382) at 201 Brotherton Lane in Ferguson in January 2004. Alumni report the building was demolished for the airport expansion (barkerreunion.blogspot.com). In 1964 Berkeley voluntarily took in Black students when the Robertson community's high school closed — relevant context for the school's demographics. The school lineage began in 1937 when the new Berkeley district took over the 'white' Kinloch High School building (see ALL-379 Hancock campus, in another batch).

name: Berkeley Middle School
historical_names: Berkeley Junior High School
district_operator: Ferguson-Florissant R-II (Berkeley School District for earlier junior-high era)
notes: Berkeley's junior high/middle school, most recently at 8300 Frost Ave. Earlier housed at 6033 Caroline Ave (the former Berkeley High campus, ALL-380) per a St. Louis Post-Dispatch listing; the move date to Frost Ave was not found. NCES-derived publicschoolreview lists 'Berkeley Middle School (Closed 2020)'. The closure coincides with the FFSD reorganization adopted October 10, 2018 (Option 2): the federal court record in the April 2019 TRO case states 'the Berkeley Middle School will continue to serve grades 3 through 5' — i.e., the middle school (grades 6-8) was ended and the building became a 3-5 elementary. Missouri Dept. of Conservation's schools roster lists 'Berkeley Middle (Now Berkley Intermediate)', indicating the school was renamed/rebranded Berkeley Intermediate School (ALL-386), which shares the 8300 Frost campus with Berkeley Elementary (ALL-385). Grades 6-8 students dispersed to the district's new sixth-grade centers (Johnson-Wabash, Wedgwood) and middle schools. 'Closed 2020' is treated as the effective end of the middle-school entity rather than a building closure.

name: Berkeley Elementary School
historical_names: Berkeley Elementary
notes: Currently operating grades 3-5 school at 8300 Frost Ave, Berkeley (NCES code 4030; 2025-26 student handbook and FFSD org chart confirm operation). The current 'Berkeley Elementary' incarnation dates to the 2018-19 FFSD grade reorganization (Option 2, adopted Oct 10, 2018): the former Berkeley Middle School building began serving grades 3-5. CAUTION: the seed describes this as the 'Current/Successor' Berkeley elementary at Frost Ave — an older Berkeley elementary lineage under the pre-1975 Berkeley School District likely existed separately (Berkeley alumni refer to an elementary school demolished for airport expansion, and the 1902-03 'Kinloch Elementary'/Hancock building at 5924 Hancock served white elementary students before the 1937 split), but no specific earlier 'Berkeley Elementary School' record was located. If that lineage matters, it may deserve a separate row; left flagged rather than conflated. Shares the 8300 Frost campus with Berkeley Intermediate (ALL-386).

name: Berkeley Intermediate School
historical_names: Berkeley Middle School; Berkeley Junior High School
notes: Current school at 8300 Frost Ave, Berkeley — has its own district site (bis.fergflor.org) and a Special School District contact listing. Missouri Dept. of Conservation's school roster explicitly lists 'Berkeley Middle (Now Berkley Intermediate)' at 8300 Frost Ave, indicating this is the renamed Berkeley Middle School (ALL-383) following the 2018-19 reorganization (opened ~2019-20 under the new name; the underlying building/program is older — date not found). NAMING OVERLAP FLAG: FFSD's grade structure calls the 3-5 band 'intermediate schools', and NCES/Title I paperwork codes the building as '4030 Berkeley Elementary School' while school-level documents call it 'Berkeley Intermediate School' — Berkeley Elementary (ALL-385) and Berkeley Intermediate appear to share the same campus and phone number. Whether they are one school with two names or two co-located schools should be clarified with the district (human follow-up recommended).

name: Holman Elementary School
historical_names: Holman School; Holman Elementary
notes: Currently operating at 8811 Harold Dr, Berkeley; per the federal court record of the 2019 reorganization it 'will continue to serve Pre-K through 2nd grade', and FFSD's 2025-26 org chart lists 'Holman Pre K-2'. Opened year not found — the building predates the 1975 district merger (it appears in the 1975 desegregation plan's school groupings as 'Holman Elementary'). NAME COLLISION FLAG: this is NOT the same school as Holman Middle School in the Pattonville R-III district (8565 Holman Dr; seed rows ALL-177/187/231/263) — different district, different building, different school.

name: Airport Elementary School - Historical Campus
historical_names: Airport School; Airport Elementary School
notes: Confirmed by the City of Berkeley's own 2023 RFP for converting the building to a community center: 'Airport Elementary School and gymnasium were constructed on this site in 1954 ... The School was closed in 2019 due to declining enrollment, and the City purchased the property in 2023.' Closure was part of the FFSD 'Option 2' reorganization adopted October 10, 2018; the City of Berkeley and residents sued unsuccessfully to block it (STLPR, April 2019). Students were absorbed into the reorganized Berkeley schools — Holman (PreK-2) and the 8300 Frost elementary (3-5) are the probable receivers, but no single successor school is documented. Building conversion to Berkeley Community Center is tracked by seed row ALL-408 (another batch). Minor address note: the city's sale ordinance lists '8249 Airport Road' while the RFP, seed, and NCES all use 8429 Airport Rd — likely a typo in the ordinance.

name: Nuroad School
historical_names: Nuroad School; Kinloch School (white); Hancock School; Little Red Schoolhouse
district_operator: Kinloch School District No. 18 (transferred to Berkeley School District in 1937)
notes: The all-white school of the 'Nuroad' community — the name of the unincorporated area of northern Kinloch Park (~1930-1937) that incorporated as the city of Berkeley (BHS alumni site documents a 1931 'Directory of Nuroad's Citizens'). A Washington University history text describes Nuroad on April 12, 1937 as a 10-room brick schoolhouse with 300+ white students, one of only two schools in Kinloch District 18 (the other being Dunbar). PROBABLE IDENTIFICATION: the same physical school as the 'Kinloch School' built 1902-03 at 5924 Hancock Ave (St. Louis County Historic Buildings Inventory: 'Kinloch Elementary School, constructed 1902-03, G. E. Reid'), which per John A. Wright's history housed both the white elementary and high school with ~300 students in 1935 — matching Nuroad's size and role; treated as probable, not confirmed. When the Berkeley district was created with the city's incorporation in August 1937, the school/building transferred to it and continued as Berkeley's white school(s) — the lineage leading to ALL-379 (Berkeley High - Hancock Campus). 'Closed' 1937 means ceased as a Kinloch-district school, not that the building stopped operating. Seed's framing (white residents' school ending in 1937) is consistent with the documented split.

name: Scudder Avenue School
historical_names: Scudder Avenue School; Scudder School
district_operator: Scudder School District (pre-1902) / Kinloch School District No. 18 (1902/03 onward)
notes: SEED FRAMING APPEARS WRONG: the seed describes Scudder Avenue School as the 'white Kinloch school after Kinloch District 18 formed in 1902' closing in 1937. Per John A. Wright's Kinloch school history (barkerreunion.blogspot.com/p/about-little-red-schoolhouse.html), the truth is nearly opposite: Scudder Avenue was the area's ORIGINAL white school 'built for children of wealthy whites' before 1902; when the new Kinloch district's white school (5924 Hancock) opened in 1903, 'Scudder Avenue School was designated for blacks and becom[ing] the property of the new Kinloch District' — a two-room structure (12'x20' and 14'x20'), eight grades, Black teachers Mamie Lightfoot and Viola Williams, enrollment seldom over 30. The St. Louis Black Heritage Trail site likewise says the Scudder Avenue School became Kinloch's (Black) elementary school in 1902. It was gone by 1937 — a Washington University account says the district then had only two schools, Nuroad and Dunbar — so the real closure is sometime between ~1903 and 1937, most plausibly when Dunbar opened 1913/14; seed's '1937' reflects the Berkeley split, not a documented school closure. POSSIBLY DISTINCT ENTITY: a separate 'Scudder School District' (rows ALL-403/ALL-503 in other batches) still existed independently — Southern School News reports Berkeley district annexed the Scudder School District on August 24 (~1959/1960); it had ~260 students (~75% Black) and no high school. Whether that district operated a school also called 'Scudder' after 1903 is unresolved — human follow-up recommended (St. Louis County school-district records).

name: Kinloch High School
historical_names: Kinloch High School
district_operator: Kinloch School District (Ferguson-Florissant R-II at the end, 1975-76)
notes: Kinloch's Black high school — the second Black high school in St. Louis County. The high school program began in 1936 inside Dunbar Elementary (see ALL-394) while the district pursued WPA funding; the dedicated 'black' Kinloch High School building opened in 1937-38 (sources split on the exact year — St. Louis Black Heritage Trail and the seed say 1937, Wikipedia's article text says 1938; infobox 'Founded 1936' refers to the program start). IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: the 'white' high school of Kinloch District 18 was simultaneously renamed Berkeley High School in 1937 when the Berkeley district split off — some sources loosely call that building 'Kinloch High School' too, but it is the ALL-378/379/380 lineage, not this one. Closed 1976 per Wikipedia after the June 7, 1975 federal court order (US v. Missouri, 388 F. Supp. 1058) annexed the Kinloch and Berkeley districts into Ferguson-Florissant effective the 1975-76 school year; ~350 students transferred to McCluer North High School (ALL-032) per Wikipedia. Building later demolished, in part for Lambert Airport expansion. Principals included Orthel T. Roberts (1936-37) and Lucye Belue (1944-74). Alumni include actress Jenifer Lewis and MO Rep. Juanita Head Walton.

name: Kinloch High School - Dunbar Campus
historical_names: Dunbar School (high-school program); Dunbar High School Program
school_type: Public High School program (housed in elementary building)
notes: This row represents the Black high-school program hosted inside the Dunbar Elementary building (ALL-395) — the seed dates (1914-1937) describe the building's lifespan, but as a 'Kinloch High School campus' the program itself ran 1936-~1938: 'in 1936, the Dunbar elementary school began hosting a high school program for local black students' (Wikipedia, citing Wright's Kinloch history and Bosenbecker); the dedicated Kinloch High School building opened 1937-38 and the program moved there (ALL-393). Kept as a separate row per the no-silent-merge rule, but flagged: ALL-394 and ALL-395 are the same physical building — this row is only the 1936-38 high-school-program use of it. Related row ALL-499 ('Dunbar School - High School Program', 1936-1937) in another batch describes the identical thing.

name: Dunbar School
historical_names: Paul Laurence Dunbar Elementary School; Dunbar Elementary School
notes: First school built specifically for Black children in Kinloch (South Kinloch Park), named for poet Paul Laurence Dunbar. Opened 1913 per Wikipedia/Kinloch history (the St. Louis Black Heritage Trail site says 1914 — treat as 1913-14). Hosted the Black high-school program 1936-~1938 (see ALL-394). CLOSURE YEAR CONFLICT: seed says 1967 but Wikipedia says 'still segregated when it closed in 1975'; the seed's 1967 matches Vernon School's well-attested closure and may be a conflation — alternatively a consolidated 'Kinloch Elementary School'/'Smith School' (SLCL Black Heritage Trail index; a Kinloch Elementary remodel study exists in the SHSMO Kinloch History Committee records S0151) may have absorbed Dunbar earlier, with the building's last use ending in 1975 when the district was dissolved. Either way the school ceased with the 1975 Ferguson-Florissant annexation at the latest; recorded 1975/probable. If it truly closed 1967, students likely went to Kinloch Elementary — unresolved, recommend human follow-up at the State Historical Society of Missouri (S0151 collection).

name: Vernon School
historical_names: Vernon School; W.T. Vernon School; Vernon Elementary School
district_operator: Ferguson School District (serving Black children of Kinloch and west Ferguson); earlier under pre-Kinloch districts
notes: The area's original Black school: a one-room frame 'schoolhouse built for the children of the servants to the whites in Kinloch' opened 1885 (Wikipedia). The St. Louis Black Heritage Trail adds nuance — it 'closed a few months later', Black children then attended the 1886 Lucas & Hunt school in Normandy, and Vernon 'moved to a number of locations in the area, served black children until the formation of the Kinloch School District in 1902, and its building remained in use as an all-black school in the Ferguson District until it was closed in 1967.' DISTRICT ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION: per that account Vernon was a FERGUSON School District school (consistent with sibling seed rows ALL-427/428/429 which list it under Ferguson), though it served Black children from Kinloch and west Ferguson — seed's 'Kinloch School District' attribution is likely wrong. Remained segregated until closed 1967; students presumably absorbed into integrated Ferguson-Florissant elementaries (the Ferguson and Florissant districts merged in 1952). The 1927 building phase is ALL-397; same school lineage, separate row per no-merge rule. 'W.T. Vernon' is the probable full name (William Tecumseh Vernon, prominent Black educator) — not independently confirmed for this school.

name: Vernon School - 1927 Building
historical_names: Vernon School; Vernon Elementary School
notes: The purpose-built 1927 Vernon School building for Black students of Kinloch and west Ferguson — 'Another Vernon School opened in 1927 to educate the black students of Kinloch and west Ferguson ... remained segregated until it closed in 1967' (Wikipedia's Kinloch article, citing Wright's 'Kinloch: Missouri's First Black City'; St. Louis Black Heritage Trail concurs on the 1927 date and 1967 closure under the Ferguson district). Same school lineage as ALL-396 — this row is the building phase; kept separate per the no-silent-merge rule. Also flagged in the dedup-review file against ALL-428 'Vernon School - Ferguson Campus' (another batch), which is very likely the same school/building under a Ferguson-district label. Building's fate after 1967 not found.

name: Our Lady of the Angels School
historical_names: Holy Angels School; Our Lady of the Angels Elementary School; Holy Angels Elementary School
district_operator: Holy Angels Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Black Catholic parish school in Kinloch. Holy Angels Parish was established in 1931 and 'opened Our Lady of the Angels Elementary School' the same year (Wikipedia); the St. Louis Black Heritage Trail confirms 'Holy Angels (now Our Lady of the Angels) Elementary School ... opened in 1931'. Wikipedia reports both church and school 'were open until 2002, making it the oldest continuing black parish in the St. Louis Archdiocese'. The '1952' date appearing in some sources (and in sibling seed rows ALL-399/ALL-512 'Holy Angels School 1931-1952') is the year the updated church building was constructed, not a school closure — flag the 1952 date on those rows as likely referring to the church rebuild. Closed with no successor school; students dispersed to remaining Catholic and public schools.

name: Berkeley School District
historical_names: Berkeley School District
notes: Seed confirmed and refined. The Eighth Circuit (515 F.2d 1365) states the Berkeley district was established in 1937 when Kinloch School District No. 18 was split in two, 'Berkeley district being white and the new Kinloch black.' The City of Berkeley incorporated July 30, 1937 with boundaries drawn to include only white families (barkerreunion.blogspot.com, citing John A. Wright Sr.; Wikipedia 'Kinloch High School'); some secondary sources date the completed split to 1938. Per the seed note, the new district took over the white Kinloch High School (Hancock Avenue building), renamed Berkeley High School. The district annexed the Scudder School District on Aug 24, 1960 (Southern School News, Oct 1960) and took in Robertson students when that high school closed in 1964 (Wikipedia 'Berkeley High School (Berkeley, Missouri)'). On June 7, 1975, the U.S. District Court (Judge James H. Meredith) ordered Berkeley and Kinloch annexed to Ferguson-Florissant R-II (388 F. Supp. 1058; SHSMO Kinloch School Desegregation Collection S0707). Member schools incl. Berkeley High School (ALL-114; Hancock, Caroline Ave, and Walter Ave campuses), Hancock School/'Little Red Schoolhouse' (5924 Hancock), Airport Elementary (built 1954, ALL-390), the former Berkeley HS turned Berkeley Middle turned Berkeley Intermediate (8300 Frost Ave), and Holman Elementary (8811 Harold Dr).

name: Berkeley School District Elementary System
historical_names: Berkeley School District schools
school_type: Public Elementary (district aggregate, not a single school)
notes: PSEUDO-ENTITY FLAG: this row is an aggregate of the Berkeley district's elementary schools, not a real named entity — kept as a search alias per no-delete rule, but Track B should not search it directly. The Berkeley district's elementary-level schools included Hancock School ('Little Red Schoolhouse', 5924 Hancock Ave — the 1902 white Kinloch School building, which housed both elementary and high school students in 1935 per the John A. Wright Sr.-based history at barkerreunion.blogspot.com); Airport Elementary (8429 Airport Rd, built 1954 — ALL-390/ALL-408); and later Berkeley Elementary/Intermediate (8300 Frost Ave, still operating under FFSD) and Holman Elementary (8811 Harold Dr, Berkeley — still operating; may be a post-1975 building, unverified). Whether the Berkeley district operated any all-Black elementary before annexing Scudder (1960) and Robertson (1964) is undetermined — the 1937 split left the Black schools in Kinloch, and Scudder/Robertson brought their own buildings. Reconstructing the full member-school list needs district records not found online; recommend human follow-up with FFSD administrative records or the St. Louis County library history collections.

name: Kinloch School District
historical_names: Kinloch School District No. 5; Kinloch School District No. 18; Kinloch District No. 18
notes: Seed's 1902 formation confirmed: at the 1902 annual spring meeting of the Ferguson School District, white residents of the Kinloch area voted to split and form their own district; a Board of Arbitration appointed by the County Superintendent ordered the creation of 'Kinloch School District No. 5, Township 46, Range 6 East' (barkerreunion.blogspot.com, quoting the ruling via John A. Wright Sr.). The district was renumbered Kinloch School District No. 18 in 1910. Seed's 'from parts of Ferguson and Scudder' is partially verified — the split came from the Ferguson district; the Scudder Avenue School (a pre-existing building) became Kinloch's Black elementary. Segregated per Missouri law: one high school and one elementary for whites, one elementary (Dunbar, est. ~1913-14) for Black children. Split in 1937-38 into the white Berkeley district and the all-Black Kinloch district despite Black residents' opposition; the all-Black district's 'separate but equal' Kinloch High School opened 1938 and ran to ~1976 (Wikipedia 'Kinloch High School'). After the 1971 DOJ suit and Liddell litigation, the U.S. District Court ordered annexation to Ferguson-Florissant on June 7, 1975 (388 F. Supp. 1058); upheld by the Eighth Circuit (515 F.2d 1365). Member schools incl. Kinloch High School (ALL-393/497), Dunbar School (ALL-395, the longest-operated all-Black school, closed 1975), Kinloch Elementary (ALL-508). ZIP corrected from seed's 63134 to 63140 (Kinloch).

name: Scudder School District
historical_names: Scudder District No. 17; Fairmont District No. 17
district_operator: Scudder School District (to 1960); Berkeley School District (after 1960)
notes: Seed's closure confirmed: the Berkeley School District voted to annex the Scudder School District on August 24, 1960 (Southern School News, October 1960, p. 14 — reducing St. Louis County's regular districts to 28). Scudder then had ~260 pupils, ~75% Black, and no high school; its high-school-age children were tuitioned to Soldan High School in St. Louis. Formation date not found — the 'Fairmont District No. 17' alias suggests a renamed 19th-century township district (seed's '1800s' is plausible but unverified). The district name relates to the Scudder area/avenue near Kinloch Park, but the 'Scudder Avenue School' (ALL-392) belonged to the Ferguson/Kinloch lineage, not necessarily this district — treat as a naming overlap, not a confirmed member school. Member school building(s) undetermined.

name: Ferguson-Florissant School District
historical_names: Ferguson-Florissant R-II; Ferguson Reorganized School District R II
notes: SEED ERROR: seed gives 1938, but Ferguson-Florissant R-II was created by the October 1951 county reorganization vote that consolidated the Ferguson, Florissant, and St. Ferdinand districts (PRiME Center/SLU; Eighth Circuit 515 F.2d 1365: 'in 1951 Ferguson, Florissant and St. Ferdinand School Districts reorganized'). The merger took effect for the 1952 school year (Living New Deal). Seed's 1938 may conflate the predecessor Ferguson Public School District or the 1939 opening of Ferguson High School. The district annexed Berkeley and Kinloch by federal court order June 7, 1975. Currently operating ~22 schools across 11 municipalities; headquarters 8855 Dunn Rd, Hazelwood (fergflor.org; NCES district 2912010). Yearbooks belong to member schools, not the district.

name: Mark Twain School
historical_names: Mark Twain Elementary School; Mark Twain Student Support Center; Mark Twain Restoration and Re-Entry Center; Mark Twain Restoration & Wellness Center
notes: SEED ERROR: 'Berkeley area' is wrong — the Mark Twain institution is in the Hazelwood/Florissant part of the district, now at 8855 Dunn Rd, Hazelwood MO 63042 (same address as district HQ), serving FFSD middle/high students as the Restoration & Wellness Center (rwc.fergflor.org). A Florissant municipal crosswalk ordinance also places 'Mark Twain School' on Derhake Road — possibly the original elementary campus, unverified. Lineage: Mark Twain Elementary School (Florissant; alumni site covers 'Classes of 1963-1981' and notes the school published only one yearbook, Spring 1974 — an unusual data point for Track B) → Mark Twain Student Support Center → Mark Twain Restoration and Re-Entry Center (renamed 2019 per Wikipedia FFSD) → Mark Twain Restoration & Wellness Center. Exact elementary opening and conversion dates not found; an FFSD board document (simbli.eboardsolutions.com) recently proposed restructuring/'Close Mark Twain Location', so current operating status should be re-verified before Track B.

name: Johnson-Wabash Elementary School
historical_names: Johnson School; Wabash School; Johnson-Wabash Elementary School; Johnson-Wabash 6th Grade Center
notes: Currently operating as Johnson-Wabash 6th Grade Center, 685 January Ave, Ferguson MO 63135 (jw.fergflor.org; NCES 291201002784 'Open' 2023-24). The name merges the earlier Johnson and Wabash schools (per seed historical names); the building sits on the same January Avenue block as Ferguson Middle (701 January). Neither the construction date nor the earlier Johnson/Wabash school histories were findable online. It was reconfigured from an elementary to a 6th-grade center in the ~2019 grade-center restructuring (Wikipedia FFSD school list) and is slated to return to K-5 in the district's 2027-28 restructuring (fergflor.org board post). Seed's 'serves portions of Berkeley' is plausible (Walnut Grove Primary explicitly lists Berkeley in its attendance communities) but boundary details unverified.

name: Walnut Grove Primary School
historical_names: Walnut Grove School; Walnut Grove Elementary School
notes: Currently operating as Walnut Grove Primary School (PreK-2), 1248 North Florissant Road, Ferguson MO 63135, serving Berkeley, Calverton Park, Florissant, and Ferguson (wgps.fergflor.org; FFSD 2023-24 directory lists it as 'Walnut Grove Elementary'). Operating by 1973 at the latest — a Pacific Standard memoir describes attending Walnut Grove Elementary in 1973. Construction/opening date not found online; recommend DESE building records or district facilities documents for the exact year.

name: Airport Elementary School - Berkeley Community Center
historical_names: Airport Elementary School; Former Airport Elementary
district_operator: Berkeley School District (1954-1975); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (1975-2019); City of Berkeley (2023-)
notes: Recorded as the school entity (the relevant yearbook target): per the City of Berkeley's August 2023 RFP for conversion, 'Airport Elementary School and gymnasium were constructed on this site in 1954... The School was closed in 2019 due to declining enrollment, and the City purchased the property in 2023.' It operated as a Berkeley district school 1954-1975, then under Ferguson-Florissant until closure in the district's 2019 restructuring. The City of Berkeley bought the ~10.4-acre parcel (Bills #4957/#4965, 2023) and is converting it into the Berkeley Community Center — seed's 'Opened 2023' describes that conversion, not a school opening (seed status 'Converted' is accurate). Students were redistributed to other FFSD elementaries (Berkeley Elementary/Intermediate and Holman are the nearest); no single successor school documented. Duplicate of ALL-390 'Airport Elementary School - Historical Campus' in another batch — same building.

name: Robertson School District
historical_names: Robertson School District
district_operator: Robertson School District (to ~1964); Berkeley School District (1964-1975); Ferguson-Florissant R-II (after 1975)
notes: Probable reconstruction: Robertson was an unincorporated, predominantly Black community west of Lambert Field (post office 1929-1958, roadsidethoughts.com; an early-1800s French settlement that became a historic Black community, per Missouri Sen. Chappelle-Nadal's 2016 history project). When the Robertson high school closed in 1964, 'the Berkeley School District voluntarily provided school bus transportation and welcomed the Robertson students into their system' (Wikipedia 'Berkeley High School (Berkeley, Missouri)'). Whether the annexation was formal in 1964 or was only a tuition/transport arrangement that later became a boundary change is unverified — recommend human follow-up with St. Louis County school district boundary records. Operated at least a high school (ALL-410) and an elementary-level school (ALL-411). The community was largely bought out/demolished for the Lambert W-1W runway expansion (1990s-2000s).

The school was still operating in Defiance during the 1948-49 school year (teacher Opal Schemmer, class of 7 boys). No closure date found — neighboring Bacon School closed June 2, 1950 in the same consolidation wave, and Defiance-area students now attend Daniel Boone Elementary (opened 1955 in New Melle, seed row ALL-587 researched in batch 19) per Wikipedia's Defiance article; closure likely fell in the 1949-1955 consolidation era but no source pins the year. The building survives as a private residence. SURPRISE: this row almost certainly duplicates seed rows ALL-582 (Walnut Grove School), ALL-583 (Sycamore School), and ALL-584 (Walnut Grove District No. 68) — all the same one-room school lineage; kept separate per no-silent-merge rule, recommend coordinator merge review.
