name: O'Fallon Public School System
historical_names: O'Fallon Public School District; O'Fallon School
district_operator: O'Fallon local district (St. Charles County); consolidated into Central School District R-II 1949
notes: Seed's 1869 confirmed by the Fort Zumwalt district's own history page: 'In 1869, a school for O'Fallon was built in the area known as Convent Park on the grounds of St. Mary's Academy. Julius Reichenstein was employed as the first teacher by the townspeople.' Lineage: O'Fallon outgrew the one-room school and built two new schools in 1910 (at the site that later held Hope High School/North Middle School on Virgil Street); a public high school operated until 1918, when a parochial high school's opening drew off enough students that public-HS students were thereafter transported to St. Charles or Wentzville. Under Missouri's 1947 district-reorganization law, voters approved combining 12 small St. Charles County districts — including O'Fallon's — into Central School District R-II on July 19, 1949; that consolidated district is today's Fort Zumwalt R-II (its first own high school opened 1960). ENTITY TYPE NOTE: classified individual_school rather than administrative_district_only because this was a small pre-consolidation town district effectively coextensive with 'the O'Fallon school' — one campus, no separately-named member schools. Successor recorded as ALL-579 (the Fort Zumwalt School District row in batch 19), the modern consolidated district that absorbed it.

name: Woodlawn Seminary
historical_names: Woodlawn Female Seminary; Woodlawn Seminary
district_operator: Private (Prof. Richard H. Pitman; Methodist Episcopal Church, South affiliated)
notes: Seed's 1878 confirmed by the Portrait and Biographical Record of St. Charles, Lincoln and Warren Counties (1895, transcribed on Genealogy Trails): 'In 1878 he erected the Woodlawn Female Seminary building and opened his present seminary, of which he is principal.' Founder Richard H. Pitman previously ran Fairview Seminary (a separate, earlier school on his farm, ~1861-1876), then was president of Howard Female College in Fayette 1876-78 before founding Woodlawn. It reported to the M.E. Church South district conference (1888 Lincoln County history: four teachers, ~50 students, full art/music courses). A Hodge Lodge cornerstone history states 'it continued until 1900' — hence closed ~1900 (probable, single informal source). Consistent with 'for forty years he educated... the girls of Northeast Missouri' across Pitman's career, and with the City of O'Fallon's note that the building was 'the former Woodlawn Seminary' when the Williams family bought it after the 1915 cyclone. No successor entity — a personal/proprietary seminary that simply ended; students dispersed to public and other private schools. Seed's 'classical education for young women' verified (a female seminary), though one biography (Caleb S. Stone) mentions a male alumnus. Seed's 'near Fort Zumwalt Park' location plausible — the site was the old Trevy/Woodlawn property near today's Fort Zumwalt Park; actual ZIP is O'Fallon 63366-era boundary.

name: Assumption School
historical_names: Assumption Parish School; Assumption BVM School; Assumption Elementary School
district_operator: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Refined seed's '1870s': per the school's own history page, the Church of the Assumption and its log schoolhouse were dedicated September 17, 1871, and the school opened a week later with 20 pupils under a lay teacher; the Sisters of the Most Precious Blood took over in September 1873 and served uninterrupted until 1991. Still operating as a K-8 school (~500 students) on Main Street, O'Fallon — actual ZIP 63366, included under 63368 community coverage. HIGH SCHOOL LINEAGE (for notes only, the row tracks the parish school): Assumption High School occupied a building dedicated 1955 and closed in 1962 when the Archdiocese opened regional St. Dominic High School — its effective successor at the HS level. Separately, the Precious Blood Sisters ran their own girls' high school and two-year college on the Convent Park campus (the 'St. Mary's Academy' referenced in the 1869 public-school account); those closed with declining vocations and the buildings were sold to the City of O'Fallon (former HS is now City Hall; college is now the police station).

name: St. Charles Community College - Dardenne Creek Campus
historical_names: Dardenne Creek Campus; One Academy Place; LU/SCC Center for Nursing and Allied Health Sciences (2013-2017)
notes: Seed's 2017 confirmed by SCC's own Fast Facts ('Dardenne Creek Campus, established in 2017'). Timeline: the 69,000 sq ft building at 1 Academy Place, Dardenne Prairie is the former Barat Academy site, purchased by Lindenwood University in September 2012; SCC leased ~26,000 sq ft for its Nursing and Allied Health program under the LU/SCC partnership from August 2013 (so SCC programming on the site predates the campus). The SCC Board approved purchase Dec. 5, 2016 and closed Feb. 24, 2017 ($9.45M) — the college's first satellite campus; officially dedicated May 2, 2018. Currently open, housing the Center for Healthy Living and the Field to Table Institute.

name: Baden Elementary School
historical_names: Baden School; Baden Elementary
notes: Continuation of the Baden public-school lineage (see 63147-06). The final Baden School building at 8724 Halls Ferry Rd was built 1907 and opened 1908 per Wikipedia's Baden neighborhood history (sourcing the city's Wayman neighborhood survey); Landmarks Association and Picture This STL date the Ittner-designed building to 1907. Closure year is conflicting: Preservation Research Office and Wikipedia say it was recommended for/closed in June 2009, while publicschoolreview.com (NCES-derived) lists 'Closed 2010' — seed's 2010 is likely a data-record year. SURPRISE: seed address '5814 Thekla Avenue' is actually the Walnut Park School (Ittner, opened Sept 1909, closed 2003) per the National Register nomination for that building; Baden Elementary's historic home is 8724 Halls Ferry Rd. The 5814 Thekla listing on publicschoolreview.com may reflect a late relocation into the vacated Walnut Park building or simply a bad address record. Successor not established — students likely dispersed to Nance Elementary (63147-02, opened 2002 nearby) and other north-side elementaries, but no direct citation found. Building is being redeveloped as Baden School Apartments (Lutheran Development Group, ldgstl.org).

name: Baden Public School
historical_names: Baden Public School; Baden School (pre-1908)
district_operator: Baden local district / St. Louis Public Schools (after 1876)
notes: WARNING: this row substantially overlaps 63147-01 — it is the same continuous school, not a separate institution. First Baden public school opened 1872 as a one-room building at Christian & Switzer; replaced in 1878 by a brick building at Church Rd & Bittner (240 students); a portable opened 1906 at Halls Ferry & Gimblin; the 'final Baden School' at 8724 Halls Ferry Rd opened 1908 and is the building associated with Baden Elementary (63147-01). Row kept separate per prompt guidance against silent merging, but a merge into 63147-01 should be considered. Separately, a 'Colored School #11' (later Aldridge School) for Black students opened in the original 1872 schoolhouse in 1878 — a distinct school that may deserve its own row in a future pass.
